```text
1	# Student Guide — Running Gitea Locally
2	
3	Welcome! This is a course fork of [Gitea](https://about.gitea.com/), a self-hosted Git service
4	written in **Go** (backend) and **Vue/TypeScript** (frontend). You'll be improving the kind of tool
5	you use every day — issues, pull requests, code review, CI/Actions.
6	
7	This guide gets you from a fresh clone to a running Gitea on your machine, backed by **SQLite** (no
8	separate database server needed). It should take ~15–30 minutes, most of which is the first backend
9	compile.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## 1. Prerequisites
14	
15	Install these before you start. Versions below are the minimums this fork is pinned to.
16	
17	| Tool | Version | Notes |
18	| --- | --- | --- |
19	| **Go** | **1.26.4+** | Backend. `go.mod` requires `go 1.26.4`. |
20	| **Node.js** | **22.18.0+** | Frontend build only (not needed at runtime). |
21	| **pnpm** | **11.0.0+** | Frontend package manager. Easiest via `corepack enable`. |
22	| **Git** | 2.x | Required both to build **and at runtime** (Gitea shells out to git). |
23	
24	> 💡 **New to Go?** Gitea's backend is written in Go. [A Tour of Go](https://go.dev/tour/) is the official interactive tutorial (~2 hours) and covers everything you need for typical backend tasks. Pay attention to goroutines and interfaces — both appear frequently in this codebase.
25	
26	> 📖 **Developer docs:** [`docs/development.md`](docs/development.md) in this repo covers the development workflow, how to run tests, database migration conventions, and the overall package structure. Read it before picking a task.
27	
28	**You do NOT need a C compiler (gcc).** This version of Gitea uses a pure-Go SQLite driver
29	(`modernc.org/sqlite`) and builds with `CGO_ENABLED=0`, so there's no MSYS2/MinGW/Xcode-tools step.
30	This is the main reason setup is painless on Windows.
31	
32	**Optional:** `make` (convenience only — every command below also has a no-`make` form), and Docker
33	(if you'd rather run the official container instead of building).
34	
35	### Installing the toolchain
36	- **Windows:** `winget install GoLang.Go` and `winget install OpenJS.NodeJS`, then `corepack enable`.
37	- **macOS:** `brew install go node` then `corepack enable`.
38	- **Linux:** use your package manager (or the official Go tarball) for Go + Node, then `corepack enable`.
39	
40	Verify:
41	```bash
42	go version      # go1.26.x
43	node --version  # v22.18+ (or newer)
44	pnpm --version  # 11.x
45	git --version
46	```
47	
48	---
49	
50	## 2. Get the code
51	
52	```bash
53	git clone https://github.com/musta55/gitea.git
54	cd gitea
55	```
56	
57	---
58	
59	## 3. Build
60	
61	Gitea is built in two halves: the frontend assets (with pnpm/vite) and the backend binary (with Go).
62	
63	### Option A — with `make` (recommended if you have it)
64	```bash
65	make build          # builds frontend + backend into ./gitea (or gitea.exe on Windows)
66	```
67	
68	### Option B — without `make` (works everywhere)
69	```bash
70	# 1) frontend assets -> public/assets/
71	pnpm install
72	pnpm exec vite build
73	
74	# 2) backend binary  (pure-Go SQLite, no gcc)
75	#    Linux/macOS:
76	CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o gitea .
77	#    Windows (PowerShell):
78	$env:CGO_ENABLED=0; go build -buildmode=exe -o gitea.exe .
79	```
80	
81	> The first backend compile takes a few minutes and produces a ~100+ MB binary. Later builds are fast.
82	
83	---
84	
85	## 4. Run (SQLite, zero config)
86	
87	Just start the web server from the repo root and let the built-in installer set everything up:
88	
89	```bash
90	# Linux/macOS:
91	./gitea web
92	# Windows:
93	./gitea.exe web
94	```
95	
96	Then open **http://localhost:3000** and you'll see the **Install** page:
97	
98	1. **Database Type:** choose **SQLite3** (the default path is fine).
99	2. Leave the rest at defaults for local dev.
100	3. Expand **Administrator Account Settings** and create your admin username / password / email
101	   (do this now so you don't have to register separately).
102	4. Click **Install Gitea**.
103	
104	That's it — you now have a running Gitea with a SQLite database at `data/gitea.db`. Log in with the
105	admin account you just created.
106	
107	> **Port already in use?** If something else owns `:3000`, start Gitea on another port:
108	> `./gitea web --port 3030` and open http://localhost:3030 instead.
109	
110	### On macOS
111	The same `./gitea web` command works — a few Mac-specific notes:
112	
113	- **Firewall prompt:** the first launch may ask *"Do you want the application `gitea` to accept
114	  incoming network connections?"* — click **Allow** (it's the binary you just built).
115	- **`permission denied`:** make the binary executable first: `chmod +x gitea`.
116	- **Gatekeeper "cannot be opened" warning:** only affects binaries downloaded from a browser, not
117	  ones you built yourself. If you ever run a downloaded release binary instead, clear the
118	  quarantine flag: `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ./gitea`.
119	- **Apple Silicon (M1–M4):** fully supported — Go produces a native arm64 binary, nothing extra to do.
120	
121	### Live-reload while developing (optional)
122	If you have `make`:
123	```bash
124	make watch          # rebuilds frontend + backend on file changes (uses air)
125	```
126	
127	---
128	
129	## 5. Try it out
130	
131	Create a repository (with "Initialize repository"), open an issue, push a branch, and open a pull
132	request so you can see the code-review UI. These are the areas most course tasks touch:
133	
134	- **Code review UI** — the diff viewer and PR review flow.
135	- **Issues / Kanban** — issue tracking and project boards.
136	- **CI / Actions** — the built-in Actions runner and workflow UI.
137	
138	---
139	
140	## 6. Running the tests
141	
142	Gitea's test suite is validated on **Linux CI**. Run it on Linux, macOS, WSL2, or the provided
143	`.devcontainer` — **not native Windows**, where a handful of unit tests fail for platform reasons
144	(symlink semantics, temp-file cleanup) rather than real bugs.
145	
146	```bash
147	# unit tests
148	CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./...
149	# or, with make:
150	make test-backend         # unit tests
151	make test-integration     # integration tests (defaults to SQLite via GITEA_TEST_DATABASE)
152	```
153	
154	Frontend tests:
155	```bash
156	pnpm exec vitest run
157	```
158	
159	---
160	
161	## 7. Common gotchas
162	
163	- **`git` not found at runtime:** Gitea runs git commands for every repo operation. Make sure `git`
164	  is on your `PATH`, not just in your IDE.
165	- **`go build` is slow the first time:** normal — it compiles ~3000 packages once, then caches.
166	- **Don't commit build artifacts:** `gitea`/`gitea.exe`, `data/`, `custom/`, and `public/assets/*`
167	  are gitignored. Keep them out of your commits.
168	- **Windows line endings:** the repo expects LF. Your editor/`.gitattributes` should keep it that way.
169	
170	---
171	
172	---
173	
174	## Contributing workflow
175	
176	All team members have write access to this repository, so the team uses a **branch-based** workflow — not forks. Here is the background and the commands.
177	
178	**Why not forks?** Forking is the standard model for contributing to open-source projects where you _don't_ have write access: you fork to your own GitHub account, clone your fork, and open a PR from your fork back to the original. You will encounter this when contributing to the upstream project. But for your course team — where everyone has write access to the shared repo — it just adds confusion: two clones on your machine, two remotes to keep in sync, merge conflicts that are harder to reason about.
179	
180	**Branch-based workflow** is what most professional teams use internally. You clone the shared repo once, create a short-lived branch for each issue, push the branch back to the same repo, and open a PR from that branch into `main`. One clone, one remote, full PR workflow.
181	
182	### For each issue you work on
183	
184	```bash
185	# One-time setup: clone the team repo (skip if already done)
186	git clone https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea.git
187	cd gitea
188	
189	# Before starting each issue: make sure you are on a fresh main
190	git checkout main
191	git pull origin main
192	
193	# Create a branch named for the issue
194	git checkout -b feat/issue-17-dark-mode      # new feature
195	git checkout -b fix/issue-42-toast-dismiss   # bug fix
196	
197	# ... make your changes, run tests ...
198	
199	# Stage and commit
200	git add <the files you changed>
201	git commit -m "feat: add dark mode toggle (#17)"
202	
203	# Push the branch to the team repo
204	git push origin feat/issue-17-dark-mode
205	```
206	
207	After pushing, GitHub shows a **"Compare & pull request"** banner on the repository page. Click it to open a PR from your branch into `main`. Fill in the description (what changed and why), reference the issue (`Closes #17`), and request a review from a teammate.
208	
209	**Branch naming:**
210	
211	| Prefix | Use for |
212	|---|---|
213	| `feat/issue-<N>-short-description` | new features |
214	| `fix/issue-<N>-short-description` | bug fixes |
215	| `chore/short-description` | docs, config, dependency updates |
216	
217	> ⚠️ **`main` is protected — direct pushes are blocked.** All changes go through a reviewed PR. If you accidentally commit to `main` locally, move your changes to a branch before pushing:
218	>
219	> ```bash
220	> git checkout -b fix/issue-42-my-fix   # create branch from your current state
221	> git checkout main
222	> git reset --hard origin/main          # revert local main to match remote
223	> ```
224	
225	**After your PR is merged**, delete the branch to keep the repo tidy:
226	
227	```bash
228	git checkout main
229	git pull origin main
230	git branch -d feat/issue-17-dark-mode
231	```
232

242	| --- | --- |
243	| How to use the tool | <https://docs.gitea.com/> |
244	| Code review process | [CONTRIBUTING.md — Code review](CONTRIBUTING.md#code-review) |
245	| Bug / issue resolution process | [CONTRIBUTING.md — How to report issues](CONTRIBUTING.md#how-to-report-issues) |
246	| Pull request conventions & PR policies | [CONTRIBUTING.md — Pull request format](CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-request-format) + [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) (commit/PR conventions) |
247	| AI policies | [CONTRIBUTING.md — AI Contribution Policy](CONTRIBUTING.md#ai-contribution-policy) + [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) |

```text
1	# Backend development guidelines
2	
3	This document covers backend-specific architecture and contribution expectations.
4	For the general workflow see [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md), and for building
5	and testing see [development.md](development.md) and [testing.md](testing.md).
6	
7	## Background
8	
9	The backend is written in Go. Web routing is handled by
10	[chi](https://github.com/go-chi/chi) and database access goes through the
11	[XORM](https://xorm.io/) ORM. Understanding how the packages depend on each other is
12	essential before contributing backend code.
13	
14	## Package design
15	
16	### Package layout
17	
18	The backend is split into top-level packages, each with a focused responsibility:
19	
20	- `build`: helper scripts used at compile time
21	- `cmd`: subcommands such as `web`, `serv`, `hooks`, `doctor`, and admin utilities
22	- `models`: data structures and database operations (XORM); keeps external
23	  dependencies to a minimum
24	  - `models/db`: core database operations
25	  - `models/fixtures`: sample data used by tests
26	  - `models/migrations`: schema migration scripts
27	- `modules`: standalone functionality with few dependencies
28	  - `modules/setting`: configuration handling
29	  - `modules/git`: interaction with the Git command line
30	- `routers`: request handlers, split into `api`, `web`, `install`, and `private`
31	- `services`: business logic that ties routers and models together
32	- `templates`: Go HTML templates
33	- `public`: compiled frontend assets
34	- `tests`: integration and end-to-end test helpers
35	
36	### Dependency direction
37	
38	Dependencies only flow in one direction:
39	
40	```text
41	cmd → routers → services → models → modules
42	```
43	
44	A package on the left may import a package on its right, but never the reverse.
45	
46	### Naming conventions
47	
48	- Top-level packages use the plural form: `services`, `models`, `routers`.
49	- Subpackages use the singular form: `services/user`, `models/repository`.
50	
51	When packages from different layers share a name, use a snake_case import alias to
52	disambiguate:
53	
54	```go
55	import user_service "gitea.dev/services/user"
56	```
57	
58	### Database transactions
59	
60	Operations that must roll back together should run inside `db.WithTx()` (or
61	`db.WithTx2()` when a value must be returned), defined in `models/db/context.go`.
62	Functions that participate in a transaction take a `context.Context` as their first
63	parameter so the transaction can be propagated.
64	
65	### XORM gotchas
66	
67	- Never call `x.Update(exemplar)` without an explicit `WHERE` clause — it updates
68	  every row in the table.
69	- Partial table migrations must use `SyncWithOptions(IgnoreDrop...)` rather than a
70	  plain `Sync`.
71	- When inserting rows with preset IDs, MSSQL requires `SET IDENTITY_INSERT` to be
72	  enabled and PostgreSQL requires the sequence to be updated afterwards.
73	
74	## Dependencies
75	
76	Go dependencies are managed with [Go Modules](https://go.dev/ref/mod).
77	
78	Pull requests should only modify `go.mod` and `go.sum` where it relates to the
79	change at hand, be it a bug fix or a new feature. Otherwise, these files should only
80	be touched by pull requests whose sole purpose is updating dependencies. Run
81	`make tidy` after any change to `go.mod`.
82	
83	Any `go.mod` / `go.sum` update must be justified in the PR description and must be
84	verified by reviewers and the merger to reference an existing upstream commit.
85	
86	## API v1
87	
88	The API is documented with [Swagger](https://gitea.com/api/swagger) and is modelled
89	on [the GitHub API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest).
90	
91	### GitHub API compatibility
92	
93	Gitea's API should use the same endpoints and fields as the GitHub API where
94	possible, unless there is a good reason to deviate.
95	
96	- If Gitea offers functionality GitHub does not, a new endpoint may be added.
97	- If Gitea exposes information the GitHub API does not, a new field may be added as
98	  long as it does not collide with a GitHub field.
99	- Existing fields should not be removed unless there is a strong reason; the same
100	  applies to status responses.
101	
102	If you notice a problem that would require a breaking change, leave a comment in the
103	code for a future refactor to API v2 (which is currently not planned) rather than
104	breaking v1.
105	
106	### Adding and maintaining API routes
107	
108	- All possible results (errors, success, and failure messages) must be documented in
109	  the swagger comments on the route.
110	- Every JSON request body must be defined as a struct in `modules/structs/` and
111	  registered in [`routers/api/v1/swagger/options.go`](../routers/api/v1/swagger/options.go).
112	- Every JSON response must be defined as a struct in `modules/structs/` and
113	  registered with its category under [`routers/api/v1/swagger/`](../routers/api/v1/swagger).
114	
115	### HTTP methods and status codes
116	
117	In general, choose HTTP methods as follows:
118	
119	- **GET** returns the requested object(s) with status **200 OK**.
120	- **POST** creates a new object (e.g. a user) and returns **201 Created** with the
121	  created object.
122	- **PUT** adds or assigns an existing object (e.g. a user to a team) and returns
123	  **204 No Content** with no body.
124	- **PATCH** edits an existing object and returns the changed object with **200 OK**.
125	- **DELETE** removes an object and returns **204 No Content** with no body.
126	
127	### Requirements for API routes
128	
129	- All parameters of endpoints that edit an object must be optional, except those
130	  needed to identify the object, which are required.
131	- Endpoints returning lists must support pagination (`page` and `limit` query
132	  options) and set the `X-Total-Count` header via `ctx.SetTotalCountHeader(...)`.
133
```

1	# Refactoring guidelines
2	
3	This document covers expectations for refactoring work. For the general workflow see
4	[CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md).
5	
6	## Background
7	
8	Gitea is a large, long-lived project. Over time the codebase has accumulated
9	outdated mechanisms, mixed frameworks, and legacy code that can cause bugs or slow
10	down new features. Refactoring keeps the codebase maintainable, but it needs to be
11	done carefully so it improves things without introducing regressions.
12	
13	## Writing a refactoring PR
14	
15	- Be forward-looking: address the root cause, not just the immediate symptom.
16	- Aim to reduce ambiguity and conflicts and to improve maintainability.
17	- Explain the rationale in the PR description: why the refactor is necessary, how it
18	  resolves the legacy problem, and its advantages and disadvantages.
19	- Keep the scope tight: preserve existing behavior where feasible and avoid bundling
20	  unrelated changes.
21	- Break large refactors into intermediate steps across multiple PRs so each one is
22	  easy to review.
23	- Include tests that verify the behavior stays correct.
24	- Prefer scheduling non-bugfix refactoring early in a milestone, so any issues
25	  surface well before a release.
26	- If there is disagreement about a refactor, escalate to the Technical Oversight
27	  Committee (TOC) for a decision.
28	
29	## Reviewing and merging
30	
31	- Keep refactoring PRs short-lived (typically no more than 7 days) with quick review
32	  cycles, and merge them promptly so they do not block on unrelated work.
33	- A non-author core member may approve and merge a refactoring PR after 7 days if the
34	  TOC has raised no objection.
35	- Accept imperfect intermediate implementations as long as the final result improves
36	  the codebase.
37	- A temporary regression caused by a necessary refactor is acceptable if it is fixed
38	  promptly afterwards.
39
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Frontend development guidelines
2	
3	This document covers frontend-specific architecture and contribution expectations.
4	For the general workflow see [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md), and for building
5	and testing see [development.md](development.md) and [testing.md](testing.md).
6	
7	## Background
8	
9	The frontend uses [Vue 3](https://vuejs.org/), [Fomantic-UI](https://fomantic-ui.com/) (built on jQuery)
10	and [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/). Pages are rendered with Go HTML templates.
11	Source files live in:
12	
13	- `web_src/css/`: CSS styles
14	- `web_src/js/`: JavaScript and TypeScript
15	- `web_src/js/components/`: Vue components
16	- `web_src/js/features/`: feature modules wired up at page load
17	- `templates/`: Go HTML templates
18	
19	## Dependencies
20	
21	Frontend dependencies are managed with [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/). The same rules as
22	for [backend dependencies](guidelines-backend.md#dependencies) apply, except the
23	relevant files are `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and new versions must always
24	reference an existing published version.
25	
26	## Framework usage
27	
28	Mixing frameworks arbitrarily makes code hard to maintain. Recommended combinations:
29	
30	- Vue3
31	- Vanilla JavaScript
32	- Fomantic-UI (jQuery), deprecated, we vendored a specific version with a lot of changes.
33	
34	Avoid combinations such as Vue with Fomantic-UI.
35	Vue components may reuse Fomantic-UI CSS classes for visual consistency.
36	Use Go templates for simple or SEO-relevant pages and Vue for complex, interactive pages.
37	Gitea uses Vue 3 **without** JSX to keep HTML and JavaScript separate.
38	
39	> [!NOTE]
40	> Fomantic-UI is not an accessibility-friendly framework. Gitea patches some ARIA
41	> behavior, but accessibility work is ongoing — prefer semantic HTML and test
42	> keyboard/screen-reader behavior where you can.
43	
44	## Gitea-specific conventions
45	
46	- Keep features in their own files or directories.
47	- Use kebab-case for HTML `id`s and classes, ideally with 2-3 feature keywords.
48	- Prefix classes to avoid short-name conflicts between different frameworks.
49	- Create a new class name when overriding framework styles instead of editing the framework's own classes,
50	  or fix the framework's source to fix all cases.
51	- Prefer semantic elements such as `<button>` over generic `<div>`s.
52	- Avoid `!important`; when it is unavoidable, document why.
53	- Prefix custom DOM events with `ce-`.
54	
55	## CSS
56	
57	Prefer Tailwind utility classes with the `tw-` prefix, and the `flex-*` layout
58	helpers over per-child margins. Gitea also ships a small set of custom helpers:
59	`gt-` for general helpers and `g-` for framework-level helpers (see
60	`web_src/css/helpers.css`); use these only when a Tailwind utility does not exist.
61	
62	Write class attributes as a single readable unit in templates:
63	
64	```html
65	<div class="flex-text-inline {{if .IsFoo}}tw-hidden{{end}}"></div>
66	```
67	
68	## TypeScript
69	
70	- Use `import type` for type-only imports.
71	- Prefer `@ts-expect-error` over `@ts-ignore`.
72	- Use the `!` non-null assertion (rather than `?.`/`??`) when a value is known to always exist.
73	- Only mark a function `async` when it actually uses `await` or returns a `Promise`.
74	  Avoid async event listeners; if unavoidable, call `e.preventDefault()` before the
75	  first `await`. For a deliberately un-awaited call, assign it: `const _promise = asyncFoo()`.
76	
77	## Data fetching
78	
79	Use the `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` wrappers from
80	[`web_src/js/modules/fetch.ts`](../web_src/js/modules/fetch.ts).
81	
82	## DOM attributes
83	
84	Avoid `node.dataset` because of its camel-casing behavior; use `node.getAttribute`
85	in new code. Never bind user-provided data directly onto DOM nodes.
86	
87	## Showing and hiding elements
88	
89	- In Vue, use `v-if` and `v-show`.
90	- In Go templates and plain JavaScript, use the `.tw-hidden` class together with the
91	  `showElem()`, `hideElem()`, and `toggleElem()` helpers from
92	  [`web_src/js/utils/dom.ts`](../web_src/js/utils/dom.ts).
93	
94	## UI component gallery
95	
96	When running Gitea in development mode, standardized UI components are available at
97	`/devtest` (for example `http://localhost:3000/devtest`). These pages are also used
98	by the e2e tests.
99
```
</details></tool-use>

module gitea.dev

go 1.26.4
===CLAUDE.md===
@AGENTS.md
===AGENTS===
- Use `make help` to find available development targets
- Run `make fmt` to format `.go` files, and run `make lint-go` to lint them
- Run `make lint-js` to lint `.ts` files
- Run `make tidy` after any `go.mod` changes
- Run single go tests with `go test -run '^TestName$' ./modulepath/`
- Run single js test files with `pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>`
- Run single playwright e2e test files with `GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='<filepath>' make test-e2e`
- Add the current year into the copyright header of new `.go` files
- Ensure no trailing whitespace in edited files
- Use Conventional Commits for commit messages and PR titles, e.g. `type(scope): subject`; `!` before the colon if breaking. Use `test` type for test-only changes.
- Never force-push, amend, or squash unless asked. Use new commits and normal push for pull request updates
- Preserve existing code comments, do not remove or rewrite comments that are still relevant
- Keep comments short, prefer same-line, explain why, never narrate code
- Prefer unit tests over integration tests when logic is testable in isolation
- Aim for sub-2s local runtime for integration and e2e tests
- In TypeScript, use `!` (non-null assertion) instead of `?.`/`??` when a value is known to always exist
- For CSS layout, prefer `flex-*` helpers over per-child `tw-ml-*` / `tw-mr-*` margins; fall back to `tw-*` utilities when specificity requires `!important`
- Include authorship attribution in issue and pull request comments
- Always add `Assisted-By` trailers to commit messages in format `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION`
- Never add `Co-Authored-By` `Signed-off-by` trailer to commit messages. Sign off must be done by a human.
```

	"gitea.dev/models/migrations/v1_8"

	"gitea.dev/modules/git"
	"gitea.dev/modules/log"
	"gitea.dev/modules/setting"

	"xorm.io/xorm/names"
)

const minDBVersion = 70 // Gitea 1.5.3

type migration struct {
	idNumber    int64 // DB version is "the last migration's idNumber" + 1
	description string
	migrate     func(context.Context, db.EngineMigration) error
}

// newMigration creates a new migration
func newMigration[T func(db.EngineMigration) error | func(context.Context, db.EngineMigration) error](idNumber int64, desc string, fn T) *migration {
	m := &migration{idNumber: idNumber, description: desc}
	var ok bool
	if m.migrate, ok = any(fn).(func(context.Context, db.EngineMigration) error); !ok {
		m.migrate = func(ctx context.Context, x db.EngineMigration) error {
			return any(fn).(func(db.EngineMigration) error)(x)
		}
	}
	return m
}

// Migrate executes the migration
func (m *migration) Migrate(ctx context.Context, x db.EngineMigration) error {
	return m.migrate(ctx, x)
}

// Version describes the version table. Should have only one row with id==1
type Version struct {
	ID      int64 `xorm:"pk autoincr"`
	Version int64 // DB version is "the last migration's idNumber" + 1
}

// Use noopMigration when there is a migration that has been no-oped
var noopMigration = func(_ db.EngineMigration) error { return nil }

var preparedMigrations []*migration

// This is a sequence of migrations. Add new migrations to the bottom of the list.
// If you want to "retire" a migration, remove it from the top of the list and
// update minDBVersion accordingly
...TAIL...

	curDBVer := currentVersion.Version
	// Outdated Gitea database version is not supported
	if curDBVer < minDBVersion {
		log.Fatal(`Gitea no longer supports auto-migration from your previously installed version.
Please try upgrading to a lower version first (suggested v1.6.4), then upgrade to this version.`)
		return nil
	}

	// Downgrading Gitea's database version not supported
	if maxDBVer < curDBVer {
		msg := fmt.Sprintf("Your database (migration version: %d) is for a newer Gitea, you can not use the newer database for this old Gitea release (%d).", curDBVer, maxDBVer)
		msg += "\nGitea will exit to keep your database safe and unchanged. Please use the correct Gitea release, do not change the migration version manually (incorrect manual operation may lose data)."
		if !setting.IsProd {
			msg += fmt.Sprintf("\nIf you are in development and really know what you're doing, you can force changing the migration version by executing: UPDATE version SET version=%d WHERE id=1;", maxDBVer)
		}
		log.Fatal("Migration Error: %s", msg)
		return nil
	}

	// Some migration tasks depend on the git command
	if err = git.InitSimple(); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	// Migrate
	for _, m := range getPendingMigrations(curDBVer, migrations) {
		log.Info("Migration[%d]: %s", m.idNumber, m.description)
		// Reset the mapper between each migration - migrations are not supposed to depend on each other
		x.SetMapper(names.GonicMapper{})
		if err = m.Migrate(ctx, x); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("migration[%d]: %s failed: %w", m.idNumber, m.description, err)
		}
		currentVersion.Version = migrationIDNumberToDBVersion(m.idNumber)
		if _, err = x.ID(1).Update(currentVersion); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}

package db

import (

type contextKey struct{ key string }

var (
	contextKeyEngine       = contextKey{"engine"}
	ContextKeyTestFixtures = contextKey{"test-fixtures"}
)

func withContextEngine(ctx context.Context, e Engine) context.Context {
	return context.WithValue(ctx, contextKeyEngine, e)
}

var (
	contextSafetyOnce          sync.Once
	contextSafetyDeniedFuncPCs []uintptr
)

func contextSafetyCheck(e Engine) {
	if setting.IsProd && !setting.IsInTesting {
		return
	}
	if e == nil {
		return
	}
	// Only do this check for non-end-users. If the problem could be fixed in the future, this code could be removed.
	contextSafetyOnce.Do(func() {
		// try to figure out the bad functions to deny
		type m struct{}
		_ = e.SQL("SELECT 1").Iterate(&m{}, func(int, any) error {
			callers := make([]uintptr, 32)
			callerNum := runtime.Callers(1, callers)
			for i := range callerNum {
				if funcName := runtime.FuncForPC(callers[i]).Name(); funcName == "xorm.io/xorm.(*Session).Iterate" {
					contextSafetyDeniedFuncPCs = append(contextSafetyDeniedFuncPCs, callers[i])
				}
			}
			return nil
		})
		if len(contextSafetyDeniedFuncPCs) != 1 {
			panic(errors.New("unable to determine the functions to deny"))
		}
	})

```text
# Testing

Gitea has four kinds of automated tests: backend unit tests, integration tests,
end-to-end (e2e) tests, and migration tests. Local runs default to SQLite, so no
extra services are required to get started.

For prerequisites see [build-setup.md](build-setup.md); for the build workflow see
[development.md](development.md).

## Unit tests

Backend unit tests live in `*_test.go` files next to the code they cover. Set
`GITEA_TEST_LOG_SQL=1` to log all SQL statements executed during the tests.

```bash
make test-backend
```

To run a single backend test, use `go test` directly or the `#` selector:

```bash
go test -run '^TestName$' ./modulepath/
make test-backend#TestName
```

Frontend unit tests run with [Vitest](https://vitest.dev/):

```bash
make test-frontend
# single file:
pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>
```

## Integration tests

Integration tests exercise Gitea against a real database. They live in
`tests/integration/` and require [Git LFS](https://git-lfs.com/) to be installed.
The database is selected with `GITEA_TEST_DATABASE`; an empty value defaults to
SQLite, which needs no external service:

```bash
make test-integration
```

Run a single integration test with the `#` selector:

```bash
make test-integration#TestName
```

If you hit errors such as a mismatched database version or SSH push failures, try a
clean rebuild first:

```bash
make clean build
```

### Running against other databases

Set `GITEA_TEST_DATABASE` together with the matching `TEST_*` connection variables.
The commands below start a throwaway database container (press `Ctrl-C` to stop and
remove it) and then run the tests against it.

#### MySQL

```bash
docker run -e "MYSQL_DATABASE=test" -e "MYSQL_ALLOW_EMPTY_PASSWORD=yes" -p 3306:3306 --rm --name mysql mysql:latest
```

```bash
GITEA_TEST_DATABASE=mysql TEST_MYSQL_HOST=localhost:3306 TEST_MYSQL_DBNAME=test TEST_MYSQL_USERNAME=root TEST_MYSQL_PASSWORD='' make test-integration
```

#### PostgreSQL

PostgreSQL tests also use a MinIO container for object storage:

```bash
docker run -e "POSTGRES_DB=test" -e "POSTGRES_USER=postgres" -e "POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres" -p 5432:5432 --rm --name pgsql postgres:latest
docker run --rm -p 9000:9000 -e MINIO_ROOT_USER=123456 -e MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD=12345678 --name minio bitnamilegacy/minio:2023.8.31
```

```bash
GITEA_TEST_DATABASE=pgsql TEST_MINIO_ENDPOINT=localhost:9000 TEST_PGSQL_HOST=localhost:5432 TEST_PGSQL_DBNAME=postgres TEST_PGSQL_USERNAME=postgres TEST_PGSQL_PASSWORD=postgres make test-integration
```

#### MSSQL

```bash
docker run -e "ACCEPT_EULA=Y" -e "MSSQL_PID=Standard" -e "SA_PASSWORD=MwantsaSecurePassword1" -p 1433:1433 --rm --name mssql microsoft/mssql-server-linux:latest
```

```bash
GITEA_TEST_DATABASE=mssql TEST_MSSQL_HOST=localhost:1433 TEST_MSSQL_DBNAME=gitea_test TEST_MSSQL_USERNAME=sa TEST_MSSQL_PASSWORD=MwantsaSecurePassword1 make test-integration
```

### Running the database test workflow with Gitea Runner

The CI database test jobs can be run locally with
[Gitea Runner](https://gitea.com/gitea/runner). Running every job is
resource-intensive and not recommended:

```bash
gitea-runner exec -W ./.github/workflows/pull-db-tests.yml --event=pull_request --default-actions-url="https://github.com" -i catthehacker/ubuntu:runner-latest
```

List the available job names, then run a single one:

```bash
gitea-runner exec -W ./.github/workflows/pull-db-tests.yml --event=pull_request --default-actions-url="https://github.com" -i catthehacker/ubuntu:runner-latest -l
gitea-runner exec -W ./.github/workflows/pull-db-tests.yml --event=pull_request --default-actions-url="https://github.com" -i catthehacker/ubuntu:runner-latest -j <job_name>
```

## End-to-end tests

End-to-end tests drive a running Gitea instance with [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/):

```bash
make test-e2e
```

To run a single e2e test file, pass it via `GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS`:

```bash
GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='<filepath>' make test-e2e
```

Useful environment variables:

| Variable | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `GITEA_TEST_E2E_DEBUG` | When set, show the Gitea server output. |
| `GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS` | Additional flags passed to Playwright, e.g. `--ui`. |
| `GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR` | Timeout multiplier (default: 4 on CI, 1 locally). |

## Migration tests

If you change a database-persisted struct under `models/` you will usually need a
new migration in `models/migrations/`. Run the migration tests with:

```bash
make test-migration
```

## Continuous integration

CI runs the unit tests, runs the integration tests against every supported database,
and tests migration from several recent Gitea versions. Please submit your pull
request with additional unit and integration tests as appropriate. Prefer unit tests
when the logic can be tested in isolation, and keep local integration and e2e tests
fast (aim for sub-2s runtime).
```

`cd /home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea; echo "=== util/error.go ==="; cat modules/util/error.go; echo "=== example model error ==="; sed -n '1,60p' models/issues/issue.go | head -60`

```text
=== util/error.go ===
// Copyright 2022 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package util

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"html/template"
)

// Common Errors forming the base of our error system
//
// Many Errors returned by Gitea can be tested against these errors using "errors.Is".
var (
	ErrInvalidArgument  = errors.New("invalid argument")        // also implies HTTP 400
	ErrPermissionDenied = errors.New("permission denied")       // also implies HTTP 403
	ErrNotExist         = errors.New("resource does not exist") // also implies HTTP 404
	ErrAlreadyExist     = errors.New("resource already exists") // also implies HTTP 409
	ErrContentTooLarge  = errors.New("content exceeds limit")   // also implies HTTP 413

	// ErrUnprocessableContent implies HTTP 422, the syntax of the request content is correct,
	// but the server is unable to process the contained instructions
	ErrUnprocessableContent = errors.New("unprocessable content")
)

// errorWrapper provides a simple wrapper for a wrapped error where the wrapped error message plays no part in the error message
// Especially useful for "untyped" errors created with "errors.New(…)" that can be classified as 'invalid argument', 'permission denied', 'exists already', or 'does not exist'
type errorWrapper struct {
	Message string
	Err     error
}

// Error returns the message
func (w errorWrapper) Error() string {
	return w.Message
}

// Unwrap returns the underlying error
func (w errorWrapper) Unwrap() error {
	return w.Err
}

// ErrorWrap returns an error that formats as the given text but unwraps as the provided error
func ErrorWrap(unwrap error, message string, args ...any) error {
	if len(args) == 0 {
		return errorWrapper{Message: message, Err: unwrap}
	}
	return errorWrapper{Message: fmt.Sprintf(message, args...), Err: unwrap}
}

// NewInvalidArgumentErrorf returns an error that formats as the given text but unwraps as an ErrInvalidArgument
func NewInvalidArgumentErrorf(message string, args ...any) error {
	return ErrorWrap(ErrInvalidArgument, message, args...)
}

// NewPermissionDeniedErrorf returns an error that formats as the given text but unwraps as an ErrPermissionDenied
func NewPermissionDeniedErrorf(message string, args ...any) error {
	return ErrorWrap(ErrPermissionDenied, message, args...)
}

// NewAlreadyExistErrorf returns an error that formats as the given text but unwraps as an ErrAlreadyExist
func NewAlreadyExistErrorf(message string, args ...any) error {
	return ErrorWrap(ErrAlreadyExist, message, args...)
}

// NewNotExistErrorf returns an error that formats as the given text but unwraps as an ErrNotExist
func NewNotExistErrorf(message string, args ...any) error {
	return ErrorWrap(ErrNotExist, message, args...)
}

// ErrorTranslatable wraps an error with translation information
type ErrorTranslatable interface {
	error
	Unwrap() error
	Translate(ErrorLocaleTranslator) template.HTML
}

type errorTranslatableWrapper struct {
	err    error
	trKey  string
	trArgs []any
}

type ErrorLocaleTranslator interface {
	Tr(key string, args ...any) template.HTML
}

func (w *errorTranslatableWrapper) Error() string { return w.err.Error() }

func (w *errorTranslatableWrapper) Unwrap() error { return w.err }

func (w *errorTranslatableWrapper) Translate(t ErrorLocaleTranslator) template.HTML {
	return t.Tr(w.trKey, w.trArgs...)
}

func ErrorWrapTranslatable(err error, trKey string, trArgs ...any) ErrorTranslatable {
	return &errorTranslatableWrapper{err: err, trKey: trKey, trArgs: trArgs}
}

func ErrorAsTranslatable(err error) ErrorTranslatable {
	var e *errorTranslatableWrapper
	if errors.As(err, &e) {
		return e
	}
	return nil
}

package issues

	"xorm.io/builder"
)

// ErrIssueNotExist represents a "IssueNotExist" kind of error.
type ErrIssueNotExist struct {
	ID     int64
	RepoID int64
	Index  int64
}

// IsErrIssueNotExist checks if an error is a ErrIssueNotExist.
func IsErrIssueNotExist(err error) bool {
	_, ok := err.(ErrIssueNotExist)
	return ok
}

func (err ErrIssueNotExist) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("issue does not exist [id: %d, repo_id: %d, index: %d]", err.ID, err.RepoID, err.Index)
}

func (err ErrIssueNotExist) Unwrap() error {
	return util.ErrNotExist
}

var ErrIssueAlreadyChanged = util.NewInvalidArgumentErrorf("the issue is already changed")

// Issue represents an issue or pull request of repository.
type Issue struct {
	ID                int64                  `xorm:"pk autoincr"`
	RepoID            int64                  `xorm:"INDEX UNIQUE(repo_index)"`
	Repo              *repo_model.Repository `xorm:"-"`
	Index             int64                  `xorm:"UNIQUE(repo_index)"` // Index in one repository.
	PosterID          int64                  `xorm:"INDEX"`
	Poster            *user_model.User       `xorm:"-"`

func NormalRoutes() *web.Router {
	r := web.NewRouter()
	r.BeforeRouting(common.ProtocolMiddlewares()...)

	r.AfterRouting(common.MaintenanceModeHandler())

	r.Mount("/", web_routers.Routes())
	r.Mount("/api/v1", apiv1.Routes())
	r.Mount("/api/internal", private.Routes())

	r.Post("/-/fetch-redirect", common.FetchRedirectDelegate)

	if setting.Packages.Enabled {
		// This implements package support for most package managers
		r.Mount("/api/packages", packages_router.CommonRoutes())
		// This implements the OCI API, this container registry "/v2" endpoint must be in the root of the site.
		// If site admin deploys Gitea in a sub-path, they must configure their reverse proxy to map the "https://host/v2" endpoint to Gitea.
		r.Mount("/v2", packages_router.ContainerRoutes())
	}

	if setting.Actions.Enabled {
		prefix := "/api/actions"
		r.Mount(prefix, actions_router.Routes(prefix))

		// TODO: Pipeline api used for runner internal communication with gitea server. but only artifact is used for now.
		// In Github, it uses ACTIONS_RUNTIME_URL=https://pipelines.actions.githubusercontent.com/fLgcSHkPGySXeIFrg8W8OBSfeg3b5Fls1A1CwX566g8PayEGlg/
		// TODO: this prefix should be generated with a token string with runner ?
		prefix = "/api/actions_pipeline"
		r.Mount(prefix, actions_router.ArtifactsRoutes(prefix))
		prefix = actions_router.ArtifactV4RouteBase
		r.Mount(prefix, actions_router.ArtifactsV4Routes(prefix))
	}

	r.NotFound(func(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {
		defer routing.RecordFuncInfo(req.Context(), routing.GetFuncInfo(http.NotFound, "GlobalNotFound"))()
		http.NotFound(w, req)
	})
	return r
}

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**`.gitignore` line 110 already ignores `/.claude/` (that line is upstream Gitea's). Shared docs must be committed for all 5 of you to have the same set, so something has to give. Which approach?**

Options:
- **Minimal .gitignore edit (Recommended)** - Replace `/.claude/` with `/.claude/*` plus `!` exceptions for the shared subfolders. Keeps everything under `.claude/` as you asked, keeps personal `settings.local.json` ignored. 4-line diff in one hunk — trivial to resolve if upstream ever touches it.
- **Put docs in docs/ instead** - Shared docs live in `docs/agent-context/` (already-tracked upstream dir, and your fork already adds docs/sprint*/ + STUDENTS.md there). Zero .gitignore changes; `.claude/` stays purely personal. Slightly less idiomatic for Claude Code.
- **Force-add the files** - Keep `/.claude/` ignored and `git add -f` each doc. No tracked-file changes at all, but every new doc needs -f and teammates' tooling may silently skip them. Fragile.

**How finely should the codebase be sliced into docs? (Each doc is capped ~120-150 lines so a session only pays for what it reads.)**

Options:
- **~14 docs: layers + domains (Recommended)** - One architecture overview, one per layer (models / modules / services / routers-web / routers-api), one per frontend area (js, templates+css, i18n), one per hot domain (issues+PR, repository, actions, auth+users), plus testing and build/tooling. Best fit for course tasks.
- **~6 broad docs (layers only)** - Architecture, backend, frontend, routing, testing, tooling. Cheapest to write and maintain, but each doc is broader so you read more tokens than you need per task.
- **~25 fine-grained docs** - One per significant subpackage (models/issues, services/pull, modules/git, web_src/js/features, ...). Most precise reads, but 5 students maintaining 25 docs diverges fastest and is a lot of upfront writing.

**How much enforcement do you want around keeping the docs in sync across 5 people?**

Options:
- **Rules + template + validator script (Recommended)** - `.claude/context/MAINTENANCE.md` with hard rules (fixed heading order, line cap, every claim cites a path, `Verified-at:` git SHA, PR-only changes), a `_TEMPLATE.md`, and a small shell script that checks the rules so drift is caught before a PR.
- **Rules + template only** - Same written rules and template, no script. Lighter to set up; relies on review discipline.
- **Rules + validator + /context slash command** - Everything above plus a `.claude/commands/context.md` slash command that walks you (or the agent) through the update protocol on demand. Most guardrails, most moving parts.

**Where should the discovery pointer live, so a fresh session finds the docs without reading them all?**

Options:
- **Both AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md import (Recommended)** - A ~6-line block at the top of AGENTS.md (so Codex/Cursor/Copilot sessions see it too) and a `@.claude/context/INDEX.md` import from root CLAUDE.md, where INDEX.md is a tiny table of doc → when-to-read. Auto-loaded cost stays under ~1KB.
- **AGENTS.md only** - One small block in AGENTS.md, no import. Smallest tracked-file footprint; the agent must choose to read the index rather than always having it.
- **CLAUDE.md import only** - Leave AGENTS.md exactly as upstream has it; only root CLAUDE.md changes. Cleanest upstream diff, but non-Claude agents get no pointer.

import {getCurrentLocale} from '../utils.ts';

/** frontend `Locale.TrN`: pick the `_1` or `_n` form for `count` and interpolate `%d` */
export function trN(count: number, form1: string, formN: string, {lang = getCurrentLocale()}: {lang?: string} = {}): string {
  const form = new Intl.PluralRules(lang).select(count) === 'one' ? form1 : formN;
  return form.replace('%d', String(count));

# Gitea Architecture Map (module path: `gitea.dev`)

> Note: this is a fork with module path `gitea.dev` (not `code.gitea.io/gitea`). Root `CLAUDE.md` is a single line: `@AGENTS.md`. `AGENTS.md` holds the repo-wide rules (make targets, Conventional Commits, `Assisted-by:` trailers, no `Co-Authored-By`/`Signed-off-by`).

## 1. Layering rules

From `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/docs/guidelines-backend.md`, the stated rule (verbatim):

> ### Dependency direction
> Dependencies only flow in one direction:
> ```text
> cmd → routers → services → models → modules
> ```
> A package on the left may import a package on its right, but never the reverse.

Package responsibilities as stated in the same doc:

- `build`: helper scripts used at compile time
- `cmd`: subcommands such as `web`, `serv`, `hooks`, `doctor`, and admin utilities
- `models`: "data structures and database operations (XORM); keeps external dependencies to a minimum" — with `models/db` (core database operations), `models/fixtures` (sample data used by tests), `models/migrations` (schema migration scripts)
- `modules`: "standalone functionality with few dependencies" — with `modules/setting` (configuration handling), `modules/git` (interaction with the Git command line)
- `routers`: "request handlers, split into `api`, `web`, `install`, and `private`"
- `services`: "business logic that ties routers and models together"
- `templates`, `public`, `tests` as expected

Naming rules (verbatim intent): top-level packages plural (`services`, `models`, `routers`); subpackages singular (`services/user`, `models/repository`). Cross-layer name collisions use a snake_case import alias, e.g. `import user_service "gitea.dev/services/user"`. This is visible everywhere, e.g. `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/routers/api/v1/repo/issue.go` imports `issues_model`, `repo_model`, `access_model`, `user_model`, `issue_service`, `issue_indexer`, `api "gitea.dev/modules/structs"`.

`modules/context` vs `services/context`: **there is no `modules/context` in this tree.** The web/API request context lives entirely in `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/services/context/` (`context.go`, `api.go`, `repo.go`, `org.go`, `private.go`, `permission.go`, `pagination.go`, `base.go`, plus `upload/`). Handlers take `*context.Context` (web) or `*context.APIContext` (API) from `gitea.dev/services/context`. The lower-level request-scoped data store is `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/modules/reqctx/datastore.go`. This is the result of an upstream refactor that moved `modules/context` up into `services/` because it needs to depend on models/services.

`docs/guidelines-refactoring.md` contains no layering rules — it is process guidance only (root-cause fixes, tight scope, split large refactors across PRs, tests required, ≤7-day review window, TOC escalation, temporary regressions tolerable if fixed promptly).

## 2. Backend conventions

**Errors.** Base sentinel errors are in `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/modules/util/error.go`: `ErrInvalidArgument` (400), `ErrPermissionDenied` (403), `ErrNotExist` (404), `ErrAlreadyExist` (409), `ErrContentTooLarge` (413), `ErrUnprocessableContent` (422). Constructors: `util.NewInvalidArgumentErrorf`, `NewPermissionDeniedErrorf`, `NewNotExistErrorf`, `NewAlreadyExistErrorf`, and `util.ErrorWrap`. Typed model errors follow a three-part pattern (see `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/models/issues/issue.go` ~lines 30-48): a struct `ErrXxxNotExist`, an `IsErrXxxNotExist(err) bool` helper, and `Unwrap() error { return util.ErrNotExist }` so `errors.Is` works across layers. There is also a translatable-error mechanism (`util.ErrorWrapTranslatable` / `ErrorAsTranslatable`) for user-facing messages.

**`db.Context` / transactions.** `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/models/db/context.go` is the core: `GetEngine(ctx)` (line 73), `TxContext` (128), `WithTx` (143), `WithTx2[T]` (156), `Insert` (179). Doc rule: operations that must roll back together run inside `db.WithTx()` (or `db.WithTx2()` when a value must be returned); "Functions that participate in a transaction take a `context.Context` as their first parameter so the transaction can be propagated." Never take a `*xorm.Session` as a parameter — pass `ctx`. There is a `contextSafetyCheck` in that file that panics in dev/test if a session-based engine is misused inside `Iterate`.

**XORM gotchas (verbatim from doc).** Never `x.Update(exemplar)` without an explicit `WHERE`. Partial table migrations must use `SyncWithOptions(IgnoreDrop...)` rather than plain `Sync`. Preset IDs need `SET IDENTITY_INSERT` on MSSQL and a sequence update on PostgreSQL.

**Registering a new table.** Each model file registers its bean in an `init()` via `db.RegisterModel(new(Foo))` (defined at `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/models/db/engine.go:112`); ~101 files do this, e.g. `models/issues/comment.go:343`, `models/repo/watch.go:42`.

**Registering a migration.** `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/models/migrations/migrations.go` holds the single ordered slice; new entries go at the **bottom**, e.g. `newMigration(342, "Add scoped workflows schema", v1_27.AddScopedWorkflowsSchema)` (line 422). The implementation goes in the current version subpackage (`models/migrations/v1_27/`), with shared helpers in `models/migrations/base/` and test scaffolding in `models/migrations/migrationtest/` + `models/migrations/fixtures/`. `minDBVersion = 70`; DB version = last migration's `idNumber` + 1. Doc: "If you change a database-persisted struct under `models/` you will usually need a new migration" — run `make test-migration`.

**Fixtures.** `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/models/fixtures/*.yml` (78 files, one per table, e.g. `issue.yml`, `repository.yml`, `user.yml`). Loaded by `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/models/unittest/fixtures.go` (`InitFixtures`, `LoadFixtures`) and `fixtures_loader.go`; the fixtures dir is resolved in `models/unittest/testdb.go` (`FixturesOptions{Dir: <root>/models/fixtures}`). `models/main_test.go` shows the consistency-check convention: `unittest.CheckConsistencyFor(t, &user_model.User{}, ...)` — adding fixture rows requires keeping counter columns (`num_issues`, etc.) consistent.

**Dependencies.** `go.mod`/`go.sum` changes must be scoped to the PR at hand and justified; run `make tidy`.

## 3. Routing

**Entry points.**
- `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/routers/init.go` — `NormalRoutes()` (line 177) mounts everything: `/` → `routers/web.Routes()`, `/api/v1` → `routers/api/v1.Routes()`, `/api/internal` → `routers/private.Routes()`, `/api/packages` and `/v2` → `routers/api/packages`, `/api/actions*` → `routers/api/actions`. Also `InitWebInstallPage` / `InitWebInstalled`.
- `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/routers/web/web.go` — `Routes()` (line 257) builds the middleware chain (gzip, sessioner, `context.Contexter()`, auth middleware, `common.PageGlobalData`, `common.BlockExpensive()`, `common.QoS()`), then `registerWebRoutes(m, webAuth)` (line 329) declares every web route via nested `m.Group("/path", func(){ m.Get(...); m.Post(...) }, middleware...)`.
- `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/routers/api/v1/api.go` — `Routes()` plus all the reusable guard middlewares: `reqToken()`, `reqSiteAdmin()`, `reqOwner()`, `reqAdmin()`, `reqRepoWriter(unitTypes...)`, `reqRepoReader(unit)`, `reqOrgMembership()`, `repoAssignment()`, `orgAssignment()`, `mustEnableIssues`, `mustNotBeArchived`, `tokenRequiresScopes(...)`, and `bind[T]` for request-body binding.
- Router abstraction is `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/modules/web/` (`web.NewRouter()`, `BeforeRouting`/`AfterRouting`/`Mount`), a thin wrapper over chi.

**Adding a web route.** Declare it inside the right `m.Group` in `routers/web/web.go` with the needed guards (`reqSignIn`, `optSignIn`, `context.RepoAssignment`, ...); implement the handler in the matching subpackage (`routers/web/repo/`, `routers/web/user/`, `routers/web/org/`, `routers/web/admin/`, `routers/web/auth/`); handler signature `func Foo(ctx *context.Context)`, set `ctx.Data["Key"] = ...` then `ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplFoo)` where `tplFoo` is a package-level `templates.TplName` constant (type at `modules/templates/htmlrenderer.go:29`) whose value is the template path under `templates/`. Forms bind via `web.Bind(forms.XxxForm{})` from `services/forms/`.

**Adding an API route.** Register in `routers/api/v1/api.go`, implement in `routers/api/v1/repo|org|user|admin|notify|packages|settings|misc/`. Handler signature `func Foo(ctx *context.APIContext)`. Conventions from the doc:
- Swagger comment block immediately above the handler: `// swagger:operation GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues issue issueListIssues` then `// ---`, `// summary:`, `// produces:`, `// parameters:`, `// responses:` (see `routers/api/v1/repo/issue.go:310` and `:552`).
- "All possible results (errors, success, and failure messages) must be documented in the swagger comments on the route."
- Every JSON request body is a struct in `modules/structs/` **and** registered in `routers/api/v1/swagger/options.go`; every JSON response is a struct in `modules/structs/` registered by category under `routers/api/v1/swagger/` (`repo.go`, `issue.go`, `user.go`, `org.go`, `package.go`, ...).
- HTTP method → status: GET 200, POST 201 + object, PUT 204 no body, PATCH 200 + object, DELETE 204 no body.
- Edit endpoints: all params optional except identifiers. List endpoints must support `page`/`limit` and call `ctx.SetTotalCountHeader(...)` for `X-Total-Count`.
- Match the GitHub API where possible; never break v1 — leave a comment for a hypothetical v2 instead.

## 4. Frontend conventions

Source layout per `docs/guidelines-frontend.md`: `web_src/css/`, `web_src/js/`, `web_src/js/components/` (Vue), `web_src/js/features/` ("feature modules wired up at page load"), `templates/`.

**`web_src/js` subdirs:** `features/` (~80 page/feature modules, e.g. `repo-issue.ts`, `repo-diff.ts`, plus `features/admin/` and `features/comp/` shared widgets), `components/` (Vue 3 SFCs, no JSX), `modules/` (cross-cutting infra: `fetch.ts`, `i18n.ts`, `init.ts`, `observer.ts`, `fomantic.ts`, `tippy.ts`, `toast.ts`, `clipboard.ts`, `shortcut.ts`, `codeeditor/`), `utils/` (pure helpers: `dom.ts`, `html.ts`, `url.ts`, `time.ts`, `color.ts`), `markup/` (rendered-content enhancement: anchors, mermaid, math), `render/`, `webcomponents/` (custom elements like relative-time, origin-url), `vendor/`.

**Wiring.** Entry point `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/web_src/js/index.ts`: imports fomantic + `../css/index.css`, then passes a flat array of `initXxx` functions to `callInitFunctions([...])` from `web_src/js/modules/init.ts`. So adding a feature = new file in `features/`, export an `initFoo()` that finds its elements (`document.querySelector`, or `initGlobalSelectorObserver` for dynamic content) and returns early if absent, then add it to the `callInitFunctions` list. Other entries: `bootstrap.ts`, `globals.ts`, `iife.ts`, `swagger.ts`, `eventsource.sharedworker.ts`, `external-render-frontend.ts`. Frameworks: Vue 3, vanilla JS, or vendored Fomantic-UI/jQuery (deprecated) — do **not** mix Vue with Fomantic-UI (CSS classes only). Go templates for simple/SEO pages, Vue for complex interactive pages.

**Conventions.** kebab-case ids/classes with 2-3 feature keywords and a framework prefix; custom DOM events prefixed `ce-`; semantic `<button>` over `<div>`; one feature per file/dir. Data fetching only via the `GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE` wrappers in `web_src/js/modules/fetch.ts`. Show/hide via `.tw-hidden` + `showElem()`/`hideElem()`/`toggleElem()` from `web_src/js/utils/dom.ts` (or `v-if`/`v-show` in Vue). Avoid `node.dataset`, use `getAttribute`; never bind user data onto DOM nodes. TypeScript: `import type`, `@ts-expect-error` over `@ts-ignore`, `!` over `?.`/`??` when a value always exists, `async` only when it awaits.

**CSS (`web_src/css`).** Prefer Tailwind with the `tw-` prefix and `flex-*` layout helpers over per-child margins; custom helpers `gt-` (general) and `g-` (framework-level) in `web_src/css/helpers.css`, used only where Tailwind has no utility; never `!important` without a comment; new class names instead of editing framework classes. Structure: `index.css` aggregator, per-area files (`repo.css`, `admin.css`, `user.css`, `org.css`, `explore.css`, `dashboard.css`, `install.css`, `actions.css`, `review.css`), and subdirs `base.css`/`helpers.css`, `modules/`, `shared/`, `features/`, `repo/`, `markup/`, `editor/`, `themes/`.

**Templates (`templates/`).** Go `html/template` with `{{template "..."}}` composition; `templates/base/` holds `head.tmpl`/`footer.tmpl`/`head_navbar.tmpl`/`paginate.tmpl`/`alert.tmpl`; `templates/shared/` holds reusable partials (`issuelist.tmpl`, `combomarkdowneditor.tmpl`, `actions/`, `secrets/`, `webhook/`); domain dirs `repo/` (234 files), `user/`, `package/`, `admin/`, `org/`, `explore/`, `projects/`, `mail/` (email bodies), `devtest/` (the `/devtest` component gallery, also used by e2e), `status/` (error pages), `swagger/`, `custom/` (site-admin override hooks). Class attributes written as one readable unit: `class="flex-text-inline {{if .IsFoo}}tw-hidden{{end}}"`.

**i18n.** Backend locale files are **JSON** in `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/options/locale/locale_<lang>.json` (29 locales; `locale_en-US.json` is the source of truth and the only file to edit — others come from Crowdin, see `crowdin.yml`). Loading/lookup: `modules/translation/translation.go` (requires the `locale_*.json` naming) and `modules/translation/i18n/`. Templates use `{{ctx.Locale.Tr "key"}}` / `TrN`; frontend mirrors it in `web_src/js/modules/i18n.ts` (`trN`). Other seeded option data lives beside it: `options/gitignore`, `options/license`, `options/label`, `options/readme`, `options/fileicon`.

3. **Integration tests** — `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/tests/integration/` (~250 `*_test.go`), against a real DB (SQLite by default, selected with `GITEA_TEST_DATABASE`); requires Git LFS. `TestMain` lives in `tests/integration/integration_test.go:78`. Shared helpers in package `tests` at `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/tests/test_utils.go`: `InitIntegrationTest()`, `PrepareTestEnv(t)`, `PrintCurrentTest(t)`, `PrepareGitRepoDirectory`, `PrepareAttachmentsStorage`, `PrepareLFSStorage`, `PrepareArtifactsStorage`, `PrepareCleanPackageData`. Test git repos and LFS data: `tests/gitea-repositories-meta/`, `tests/gitea-lfs-meta/`, `tests/testdata/`. Run `make test-integration`, `make test-integration#TestName`.
4. **E2E tests** — Playwright, `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/tests/e2e/*.test.ts` with shared helpers in `tests/e2e/utils.ts`; config `playwright.config.ts`.
