# Gitea Architecture Map (module path: `gitea.dev`)

&gt; Note: this is a fork with module path `gitea.dev` (not `code.gitea.io/gitea`). Root `CLAUDE.md` is a single line: `@AGENTS.md`. `AGENTS.md` holds the repo-wide rules (make targets, Conventional Commits, `Assisted-by:` trailers, no `Co-Authored-By`/`Signed-off-by`).

## 1. Layering rules

From `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/docs/guidelines-backend.md`, the stated rule (verbatim):

&gt; ### Dependency direction
&gt; Dependencies only flow in one direction:
&gt; ```text
&gt; cmd → routers → services → models → modules
&gt; ```
&gt; A package on the left may import a package on its right, but never the reverse.

Package responsibilities as stated in the same doc:

- `build`: helper scripts used at compile time
- `cmd`: subcommands such as `web`, `serv`, `hooks`, `doctor`, and admin utilities
- `models`: "data structures and database operations (XORM); keeps external dependencies to a minimum" — with `models/db` (core database operations), `models/fixtures` (sample data used by tests), `models/migrations` (schema migration scripts)
- `modules`: "standalone functionality with few dependencies" — with `modules/setting` (configuration handling), `modules/git` (interaction with the Git command line)
- `routers`: "request handlers, split into `api`, `web`, `install`, and `private`"
- `services`: "business logic that ties routers and models together"
- `templates`, `public`, `tests` as expected

Naming rules (verbatim intent): top-level packages plural (`services`, `models`, `routers`); subpackages singular (`services/user`, `models/repository`). Cross-layer name collisions use a snake_case import alias, e.g. `import user_service "gitea.dev/services/user"`. This is visible everywhere, e.g. `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/routers/api/v1/repo/issue.go` imports `issues_model`, `repo_model`, `access_model`, `user_model`, `issue_service`, `issue_indexer`, `api "gitea.dev/modules/structs"`.

`modules/context` vs `services/context`: **there is no `modules/context` in this tree.** The web/API request context lives entirely in `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/services/context/` (`context.go`, `api.go`, `repo.go`, `org.go`, `private.go`, `permission.go`, `pagination.go`, `base.go`, plus `upload/`). Handlers take `*context.Context` (web) or `*context.APIContext` (API) from `gitea.dev/services/context`. The lower-level request-scoped data store is `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/modules/reqctx/datastore.go`. This is the result of an upstream refactor that moved `modules/context` up into `services/` because it needs to depend on models/services.

`docs/guidelines-refactoring.md` contains no layering rules — it is process guidance only (root-cause fixes, tight scope, split large refactors across PRs, tests required, ≤7-day review window, TOC escalation, temporary regressions tolerable if fixed promptly).

## 2. Backend conventions

**Errors.** Base sentinel errors are in `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/modules/util/error.go`: `ErrInvalidArgument` (400), `ErrPermissionDenied` (403), `ErrNotExist` (404), `ErrAlreadyExist` (409), `ErrContentTooLarge` (413), `ErrUnprocessableContent` (422). Constructors: `util.NewInvalidArgumentErrorf`, `NewPermissionDeniedErrorf`, `NewNotExistErrorf`, `NewAlreadyExistErrorf`, and `util.ErrorWrap`. Typed model errors follow a three-part pattern (see `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/models/issues/issue.go` ~lines 30-48): a struct `ErrXxxNotExist`, an `IsErrXxxNotExist(err) bool` helper, and `Unwrap() error { return util.ErrNotExist }` so `errors.Is` works across layers. There is also a translatable-error mechanism (`util.ErrorWrapTranslatable` / `ErrorAsTranslatable`) for user-facing messages.

**`db.Context` / transactions.** `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/models/db/context.go` is the core: `GetEngine(ctx)` (line 73), `TxContext` (128), `WithTx` (143), `WithTx2[T]` (156), `Insert` (179). Doc rule: operations that must roll back together run inside `db.WithTx()` (or `db.WithTx2()` when a value must be returned); "Functions that participate in a transaction take a `context.Context` as their first parameter so the transaction can be propagated." Never take a `*xorm.Session` as a parameter — pass `ctx`. There is a `contextSafetyCheck` in that file that panics in dev/test if a session-based engine is misused inside `Iterate`.

**XORM gotchas (verbatim from doc).** Never `x.Update(exemplar)` without an explicit `WHERE`. Partial table migrations must use `SyncWithOptions(IgnoreDrop...)` rather than plain `Sync`. Preset IDs need `SET IDENTITY_INSERT` on MSSQL and a sequence update on PostgreSQL.

**Registering a new table.** Each model file registers its bean in an `init()` via `db.RegisterModel(new(Foo))` (defined at `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/models/db/engine.go:112`); ~101 files do this, e.g. `models/issues/comment.go:343`, `models/repo/watch.go:42`.

**Registering a migration.** `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/models/migrations/migrations.go` holds the single ordered slice; new entries go at the **bottom**, e.g. `newMigration(342, "Add scoped workflows schema", v1_27.AddScopedWorkflowsSchema)` (line 422). The implementation goes in the current version subpackage (`models/migrations/v1_27/`), with shared helpers in `models/migrations/base/` and test scaffolding in `models/migrations/migrationtest/` + `models/migrations/fixtures/`. `minDBVersion = 70`; DB version = last migration's `idNumber` + 1. Doc: "If you change a database-persisted struct under `models/` you will usually need a new migration" — run `make test-migration`.

**Fixtures.** `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/models/fixtures/*.yml` (78 files, one per table, e.g. `issue.yml`, `repository.yml`, `user.yml`). Loaded by `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/models/unittest/fixtures.go` (`InitFixtures`, `LoadFixtures`) and `fixtures_loader.go`; the fixtures dir is resolved in `models/unittest/testdb.go` (`FixturesOptions{Dir: &lt;root&gt;/models/fixtures}`). `models/main_test.go` shows the consistency-check convention: `unittest.CheckConsistencyFor(t, &amp;user_model.User{}, ...)` — adding fixture rows requires keeping counter columns (`num_issues`, etc.) consistent.

**Dependencies.** `go.mod`/`go.sum` changes must be scoped to the PR at hand and justified; run `make tidy`.

## 3. Routing

**Entry points.**
- `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/routers/init.go` — `NormalRoutes()` (line 177) mounts everything: `/` → `routers/web.Routes()`, `/api/v1` → `routers/api/v1.Routes()`, `/api/internal` → `routers/private.Routes()`, `/api/packages` and `/v2` → `routers/api/packages`, `/api/actions*` → `routers/api/actions`. Also `InitWebInstallPage` / `InitWebInstalled`.
- `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/routers/web/web.go` — `Routes()` (line 257) builds the middleware chain (gzip, sessioner, `context.Contexter()`, auth middleware, `common.PageGlobalData`, `common.BlockExpensive()`, `common.QoS()`), then `registerWebRoutes(m, webAuth)` (line 329) declares every web route via nested `m.Group("/path", func(){ m.Get(...); m.Post(...) }, middleware...)`.
- `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/routers/api/v1/api.go` — `Routes()` plus all the reusable guard middlewares: `reqToken()`, `reqSiteAdmin()`, `reqOwner()`, `reqAdmin()`, `reqRepoWriter(unitTypes...)`, `reqRepoReader(unit)`, `reqOrgMembership()`, `repoAssignment()`, `orgAssignment()`, `mustEnableIssues`, `mustNotBeArchived`, `tokenRequiresScopes(...)`, and `bind[T]` for request-body binding.
- Router abstraction is `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/modules/web/` (`web.NewRouter()`, `BeforeRouting`/`AfterRouting`/`Mount`), a thin wrapper over chi.

**Adding a web route.** Declare it inside the right `m.Group` in `routers/web/web.go` with the needed guards (`reqSignIn`, `optSignIn`, `context.RepoAssignment`, ...); implement the handler in the matching subpackage (`routers/web/repo/`, `routers/web/user/`, `routers/web/org/`, `routers/web/admin/`, `routers/web/auth/`); handler signature `func Foo(ctx *context.Context)`, set `ctx.Data["Key"] = ...` then `ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplFoo)` where `tplFoo` is a package-level `templates.TplName` constant (type at `modules/templates/htmlrenderer.go:29`) whose value is the template path under `templates/`. Forms bind via `web.Bind(forms.XxxForm{})` from `services/forms/`.

**Adding an API route.** Register in `routers/api/v1/api.go`, implement in `routers/api/v1/repo|org|user|admin|notify|packages|settings|misc/`. Handler signature `func Foo(ctx *context.APIContext)`. Conventions from the doc:
- Swagger comment block immediately above the handler: `// swagger:operation GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues issue issueListIssues` then `// ---`, `// summary:`, `// produces:`, `// parameters:`, `// responses:` (see `routers/api/v1/repo/issue.go:310` and `:552`).
- "All possible results (errors, success, and failure messages) must be documented in the swagger comments on the route."
- Every JSON request body is a struct in `modules/structs/` **and** registered in `routers/api/v1/swagger/options.go`; every JSON response is a struct in `modules/structs/` registered by category under `routers/api/v1/swagger/` (`repo.go`, `issue.go`, `user.go`, `org.go`, `package.go`, ...).
- HTTP method → status: GET 200, POST 201 + object, PUT 204 no body, PATCH 200 + object, DELETE 204 no body.
- Edit endpoints: all params optional except identifiers. List endpoints must support `page`/`limit` and call `ctx.SetTotalCountHeader(...)` for `X-Total-Count`.
- Match the GitHub API where possible; never break v1 — leave a comment for a hypothetical v2 instead.

## 4. Frontend conventions

Source layout per `docs/guidelines-frontend.md`: `web_src/css/`, `web_src/js/`, `web_src/js/components/` (Vue), `web_src/js/features/` ("feature modules wired up at page load"), `templates/`.

**`web_src/js` subdirs:** `features/` (~80 page/feature modules, e.g. `repo-issue.ts`, `repo-diff.ts`, plus `features/admin/` and `features/comp/` shared widgets), `components/` (Vue 3 SFCs, no JSX), `modules/` (cross-cutting infra: `fetch.ts`, `i18n.ts`, `init.ts`, `observer.ts`, `fomantic.ts`, `tippy.ts`, `toast.ts`, `clipboard.ts`, `shortcut.ts`, `codeeditor/`), `utils/` (pure helpers: `dom.ts`, `html.ts`, `url.ts`, `time.ts`, `color.ts`), `markup/` (rendered-content enhancement: anchors, mermaid, math), `render/`, `webcomponents/` (custom elements like relative-time, origin-url), `vendor/`.

**Wiring.** Entry point `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/web_src/js/index.ts`: imports fomantic + `../css/index.css`, then passes a flat array of `initXxx` functions to `callInitFunctions([...])` from `web_src/js/modules/init.ts`. So adding a feature = new file in `features/`, export an `initFoo()` that finds its elements (`document.querySelector`, or `initGlobalSelectorObserver` for dynamic content) and returns early if absent, then add it to the `callInitFunctions` list. Other entries: `bootstrap.ts`, `globals.ts`, `iife.ts`, `swagger.ts`, `eventsource.sharedworker.ts`, `external-render-frontend.ts`. Frameworks: Vue 3, vanilla JS, or vendored Fomantic-UI/jQuery (deprecated) — do **not** mix Vue with Fomantic-UI (CSS classes only). Go templates for simple/SEO pages, Vue for complex interactive pages.

**Conventions.** kebab-case ids/classes with 2-3 feature keywords and a framework prefix; custom DOM events prefixed `ce-`; semantic `&lt;button&gt;` over `&lt;div&gt;`; one feature per file/dir. Data fetching only via the `GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE` wrappers in `web_src/js/modules/fetch.ts`. Show/hide via `.tw-hidden` + `showElem()`/`hideElem()`/`toggleElem()` from `web_src/js/utils/dom.ts` (or `v-if`/`v-show` in Vue). Avoid `node.dataset`, use `getAttribute`; never bind user data onto DOM nodes. TypeScript: `import type`, `@ts-expect-error` over `@ts-ignore`, `!` over `?.`/`??` when a value always exists, `async` only when it awaits.

**CSS (`web_src/css`).** Prefer Tailwind with the `tw-` prefix and `flex-*` layout helpers over per-child margins; custom helpers `gt-` (general) and `g-` (framework-level) in `web_src/css/helpers.css`, used only where Tailwind has no utility; never `!important` without a comment; new class names instead of editing framework classes. Structure: `index.css` aggregator, per-area files (`repo.css`, `admin.css`, `user.css`, `org.css`, `explore.css`, `dashboard.css`, `install.css`, `actions.css`, `review.css`), and subdirs `base.css`/`helpers.css`, `modules/`, `shared/`, `features/`, `repo/`, `markup/`, `editor/`, `themes/`.

**Templates (`templates/`).** Go `html/template` with `{{template "..."}}` composition; `templates/base/` holds `head.tmpl`/`footer.tmpl`/`head_navbar.tmpl`/`paginate.tmpl`/`alert.tmpl`; `templates/shared/` holds reusable partials (`issuelist.tmpl`, `combomarkdowneditor.tmpl`, `actions/`, `secrets/`, `webhook/`); domain dirs `repo/` (234 files), `user/`, `package/`, `admin/`, `org/`, `explore/`, `projects/`, `mail/` (email bodies), `devtest/` (the `/devtest` component gallery, also used by e2e), `status/` (error pages), `swagger/`, `custom/` (site-admin override hooks). Class attributes written as one readable unit: `class="flex-text-inline {{if .IsFoo}}tw-hidden{{end}}"`.

**i18n.** Backend locale files are **JSON** in `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/options/locale/locale_&lt;lang&gt;.json` (29 locales; `locale_en-US.json` is the source of truth and the only file to edit — others come from Crowdin, see `crowdin.yml`). Loading/lookup: `modules/translation/translation.go` (requires the `locale_*.json` naming) and `modules/translation/i18n/`. Templates use `{{ctx.Locale.Tr "key"}}` / `TrN`; frontend mirrors it in `web_src/js/modules/i18n.ts` (`trN`). Other seeded option data lives beside it: `options/gitignore`, `options/license`, `options/label`, `options/readme`, `options/fileicon`.

## 5. Testing

Four tiers per `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/docs/testing.md`.

1. **Backend unit tests** — `*_test.go` colocated with the code. Packages that touch the DB add a `main_test.go` with `func TestMain(m *testing.M) { unittest.MainTest(m) }`. Helper package: `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/models/unittest/` — `MainTest(m, *TestOptions{FixtureFiles, SetUp, TearDown})` in `testdb.go:41`, `PrepareTestDatabase()`, `AssertExistsAndLoadBean`, `CheckConsistencyFor` (`consistency.go`), `mock_http.go`, `fscopy.go`. For handler-level unit tests there is `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/services/contexttest/context_tests.go` (builds a fake `*context.Context`/`*APIContext`). `GITEA_TEST_LOG_SQL=1` logs SQL. Run: `make test-backend`, `make test-backend#TestName`, `go test -run '^TestName$' ./modulepath/`.
2. **Frontend unit tests** — Vitest, `*.test.ts` next to source (`web_src/js/utils/dom.test.ts`, `web_src/js/modules/fetch.test.ts`); config `vitest.config.ts`, setup `web_src/js/vitest.setup.ts`, helpers `web_src/js/utils/testhelper.ts`. Run `make test-frontend` or `pnpm exec vitest &lt;filter&gt;`.
3. **Integration tests** — `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/tests/integration/` (~250 `*_test.go`), against a real DB (SQLite by default, selected with `GITEA_TEST_DATABASE`); requires Git LFS. `TestMain` lives in `tests/integration/integration_test.go:78`. Shared helpers in package `tests` at `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/tests/test_utils.go`: `InitIntegrationTest()`, `PrepareTestEnv(t)`, `PrintCurrentTest(t)`, `PrepareGitRepoDirectory`, `PrepareAttachmentsStorage`, `PrepareLFSStorage`, `PrepareArtifactsStorage`, `PrepareCleanPackageData`. Test git repos and LFS data: `tests/gitea-repositories-meta/`, `tests/gitea-lfs-meta/`, `tests/testdata/`. Run `make test-integration`, `make test-integration#TestName`.
4. **E2E tests** — Playwright, `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/tests/e2e/*.test.ts` with shared helpers in `tests/e2e/utils.ts`; config `playwright.config.ts`. Run `make test-e2e`, single file via `GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='&lt;filepath&gt;'`; env knobs `GITEA_TEST_E2E_DEBUG`, `GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR`.
5. **Migration tests** — `make test-migration`, driven by `models/migrations/migrations_test.go` + `models/migrations/migrationtest/`.

Policy (AGENTS.md + testing.md): prefer unit tests when logic is testable in isolation; keep integration/e2e sub-2s locally. Fuzz targets in `tests/fuzz/`.

## 6. Directory inventory

### `models/` — persistence layer (XORM beans + queries)
- **Infrastructure:** `db` (engine, `GetEngine`, `WithTx`, iterate/list/paginator, drivers, install), `migrations` (versioned schema scripts `v1_6`…`v1_27` + `base`, `migrationtest`, `fixtures`), `fixtures` (78 YAML seed files), `unittest` (test DB + fixture harness), `dbfs` (DB-backed virtual filesystem, used for Actions logs), `shared/types` (leaf types shared across model packages), `unit` (repo unit/feature enum: code, issues, wiki, …), `system` (settings, app state, notices), `admin` (background `Task` records).
- **Auth/user domain:** `user` (User, email addresses, settings, redirects, followers), `auth` (login sources, tokens, OAuth2, WebAuthn, TOTP, scopes), `asymkey` (SSH keys, deploy keys, GPG keys/verification), `avatars` (avatar email hashes), `perm` + `perm/access` (access modes, computed repo permissions), `organization` (orgs, teams, team units, membership).
- **Repository domain:** `repo` (Repository, collaboration, watch, star, fork, release, attachment, topic, archive, license, upload, mirror, pushmirror), `git` (branch/tag/protected-branch/commit-status records), `gituser` (mapping git identities to users), `renderhelper` (context objects for rendering markup in repo/comment/wiki scope), `webhook` (hook definitions + delivery tasks), `secret` (repo/org secrets).
- **Issues/PR domain:** `issues` (Issue, Comment, Label, Milestone, PullRequest, Review, Reaction, Assignees, Dependency, Stopwatch/TrackedTime, ContentHistory, IssuePin/Watch), `pull` (auto-merge scheduling), `project` (project boards/columns).
- **Other domains:** `actions` (CI runs, jobs, tasks, runners, artifacts, schedules, variables), `packages` (package registry metadata, plus per-ecosystem subdirs), `activities` (action feed, notifications, heatmap, statistics).

### `modules/` — leaf utilities, minimal deps (~85 pkgs; clusters)
- **Config &amp; runtime:** `setting` (all config parsing), `graceful` (graceful restart/shutdown), `process` (process manager), `reqctx` (request-scoped datastore), `log`, `gtprof` (tracing), `pprof`, `metrics`, `updatechecker`, `dump`, `tempdir`, `test`/`testlogger` (test helpers), `consts`.
- **Git &amp; repo mechanics:** `git` (git CLI wrapper, the biggest module), `gitrepo` (repo-path-aware git access), `repository` (repo creation/init/adopt helpers), `lfs` + `lfstransfer`, `analyze` (language detection), `highlight`, `charset`, `typesniffer`, `commitstatus`, `references` (issue-reference parsing in commits).
- **Web plumbing:** `web` (chi router wrapper, `Bind`), `httplib`, `httpcache`, `session`, `templates` (Go template renderer + all template funcs), `markup` (markdown/orgmode/asciicast/external renderers), `htmlutil`, `public` (embedded/static assets), `assetfs`, `svg`, `emoji`, `fileicon`, `paginator`, `sitemap`, `eventsource`, `translation` (+`translation/i18n`), `options` (embedded `options/` data), `structs` (all API DTOs — the swagger models).
- **Storage &amp; async:** `storage` (local/minio/azure), `cache` + `cachegroup`, `nosql` (redis/leveldb), `queue`, `globallock`, `indexer` (`code`, `issues`, `stats` backends: bleve, elasticsearch, meilisearch, db), `zstd`, `container`/`optional`/`util`/`json`/`timeutil`/`base` (generic helpers), `csv`, `glob`, `regexplru`.
- **Integrations &amp; security:** `auth` (password hashing/complexity, WebAuthn plumbing), `secret`, `hostmatcher`, `proxy`/`proxyprotocol`, `ssh` (builtin SSH server), `private` (internal API client), `webhook`, `migration` (upstream-migration interfaces/schemas), `packages` (per-ecosystem metadata parsers), `actions`, `hcaptcha`/`mcaptcha`/`recaptcha`/`turnstile`, `avatar`, `badge`, `label`, `issue` (template parsing), `user`, `system`, `validation`, `uri`, `generate`, `tailmsg`.

### `services/` — business logic orchestration
- **Request plumbing:** `context` (**the** web/API request context — `Context`, `APIContext`, repo/org/user assignment, permissions, pagination, response helpers, `upload/`), `contexttest` (fake contexts for tests), `forms` (all binding/validation form structs), `convert` (model → `modules/structs` API DTO conversion).
- **Auth/user:** `auth` (all auth methods + source management, `auth/source/{db,ldap,oauth2,pam,smtp,sspi}`), `oauth2_provider`, `externalaccount`, `user` (create/update/delete/rename), `org` (org+team lifecycle), `asymkey` (key add/verify, commit signing), `secrets`.
- **Repository:** `repository` (create/fork/adopt/transfer/delete/push-update, branch &amp; file editing), `git` (higher-level git ops), `gitdiff` (diff parsing/rendering), `mirror`, `wiki`, `release`, `attachment`, `webhook` (delivery), `feed`, `webtheme`.
- **Issues/PR:** `issue` (issue/comment/label/milestone/assignee ops, `issue/template`), `pull` (PR create/merge/review/patch checking), `automerge` + `automergequeue`, `agit` (AGit-flow push-to-create-PR), `projects`, `markup` (render pipeline for comments/files).
- **Infrastructure/background:** `actions` (workflow scheduling, job dispatch, log handling), `cron` (scheduled tasks), `task` (async task runner), `migrations` (import from GitHub/GitLab/Gitea/Gogs/OneDev/Codebase), `versioned_migration` (bridge that runs `models/migrations`), `mailer` (+ `mailer/token`), `notify` + `uinotification`, `indexer` (index update coordination), `doctor` (self-check/repair), `packages`, `lfs`.

### `routers/` — HTTP handlers
- `init.go` — global init + `NormalRoutes()` route tree.
- `web/` — HTML UI: `web.go` (route table), `base.go`, `home.go`, `githttp.go` (git-over-HTTP), `goget.go`, `passkey.go`, `webfinger.go`, `nodeinfo.go`, `metrics.go`, `swagger_json.go`; subpackages `repo/`, `user/`, `org/`, `admin/`, `auth/`, `explore/`, `feed/`, `events/` (SSE), `misc/`, `healthcheck/`, `devtest/`, `shared/`.
- `api/v1/` — REST API: `api.go` (route table + guards), `repo/`, `org/`, `user/`, `admin/`, `notify/`, `packages/`, `settings/`, `misc/`, `activitypub/`, `shared/`, `utils/` (pagination helpers), `swagger/` (response/option registration for go-swagger).
- `api/packages/` — one subpackage per package registry (npm, nuget, maven, pypi, container, cargo, debian, rpm, …) + `helper/`.
- `api/actions/` — Actions runner protocol, artifacts (v1 + v4), job summaries, `ping/`, `runner/`.
- `private/` — internal API called by `cmd/serv` and git hooks (pre/post/proc-receive, key checks, restore, manager).
- `install/` — the first-run installer routes/pages.
- `common/` — middleware and shared handlers used by both web and API (auth verification, `blockexpensive`, `qos`, `compare`, `codesearch`, `db`, `errpage`, `middleware`).
- `utils/` — small shared helpers.

### `cmd/` — CLI subcommands
Flat package (`web.go`, `serv.go`, `hook.go`, `admin*.go`, `doctor.go`, `dump.go`, `migrate*.go`, `keys.go`, `manager*.go`, `actions.go`, `embedded.go`, `generate.go`, `restore_repo.go`, `mailer.go`, `docs.go`) plus `cmdtest/`. Entry point is `/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/main.go`.</result>

# Plan: `.claude-students/` — a shared, per-subpackage context map for the CSCI-435 Gitea fork

## Context

Five students share this Gitea fork (`CSCI-435-SE/gitea`) for a semester of feature work and bug
fixes, on token-limited plans. Gitea is ~85 `modules/` packages, ~25 `models/` packages, ~35
`services/` packages and a 4-tier test suite; every session currently re-discovers the same
structure from scratch, which is the single largest avoidable token cost. `AGENTS.md` (20 lines)
covers commit/lint mechanics only — it says nothing about *where* anything lives.

This plan creates one universal, git-tracked set of short per-subpackage docs so a session reads
1–3 targeted files instead of grepping the tree, plus **strict, enforceable update rules** so five
maintainers don't drift into five divergent versions.

Two hard constraints shape the design:

1. **Upstream-mergeable.** The work must be one deletable folder plus a 4-line footprint in
   tracked files. Removal is `rm -rf .claude-students/` and reverting those 4 lines.
2. **`.claude/` is unusable.** `.gitignore:110` is `/.claude/` — upstream Gitea's own line — so
   anything there is untracked and never reaches teammates. Verified `.claude-students/` is **not**
   ignored (`git check-ignore` → exit 1).

**Accepted tradeoff of the non-`.claude` name:** Claude Code auto-loads skills and slash commands
only from `.claude/`, so this folder gets none. Discovery is instead a `@`-import of a tiny index,
which works from any path. No slash command; `MAINTENANCE.md` is the protocol.

---

## Footprint on tracked files (the entire diff outside the new folder)

`CLAUDE.md` — currently one line, becomes two:
```
 @AGENTS.md
+@.claude-students/INDEX.md
```

`AGENTS.md` — one bullet appended to the existing flat bullet list, matching its style:
```
+- Read `.claude-students/INDEX.md` first: it maps each subpackage to a short context doc. Read the
+  1-3 docs matching your task instead of exploring the tree. Update them per
+  `.claude-students/MAINTENANCE.md` whenever you find one wrong.
```

Nothing else is touched. No `Makefile` target, no `.gitignore` edit, no CI wiring.

---

## Folder layout

```
.claude-students/
  README.md          what this folder is, who owns it, how to delete it cleanly
  INDEX.md           <= 40 lines. Auto-loaded every session. Path glob -> doc, one row each.
  MAINTENANCE.md     the strict rules (below). Read before editing any doc.
  _TEMPLATE.md       the only permitted doc skeleton.
  check.sh           validator; must pass before any PR touching this folder.
  docs/
    architecture.md
    ...one doc per subpackage/subunit
```

`INDEX.md` is the only always-loaded file, so it is a routing table and nothing else — no prose:

| Working on | Read |
| --- | --- |
| `models/db`, transactions, queries | `docs/models-db.md` |
| `services/pull`, `services/gitdiff`, review UI | `docs/services-pull-and-gitdiff.md` |

---

## Doc template (`_TEMPLATE.md`)

Fixed frontmatter + fixed H2 set, in order. `check.sh` rejects extra, missing or reordered H2s.

```markdown
---
scope: services/pull, services/automerge, services/agit
verified-at: c0092050a4
---

# services/pull — pull request lifecycle

**Read when:** creating/merging PRs, review state, patch checking.
**Not here:** diff rendering -> `services-pull-and-gitdiff.md`; PR rows -> `models-issues.md`.

## Responsibilities
## Key files
| Path | What it holds |
## Conventions & invariants
## Recipes
## Gotchas
## Related
```

- `scope:` lists the repo paths this doc owns. Every path must exist; scopes must not overlap
  another doc's — that is what makes "one fact, one home" checkable.
- `verified-at:` is the short SHA the doc was last checked against.
- `Key files` cites `path/file.go:42`, never pasted source.

---

## The strict rules (`MAINTENANCE.md`)

Written as numbered, checkable rules. The mechanically checkable ones are enforced by `check.sh`.

**Scope discipline**
1. Upstream docs win. `docs/guidelines-backend.md`, `docs/guidelines-frontend.md`,
   `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `AGENTS.md` are authoritative; these docs summarise and link, never
   contradict. A conflict is a bug in *this* folder.
2. A fact lives in exactly **one** doc — the one whose `scope:` owns that path. Elsewhere, link.
3. Record a fact only if it (a) took more than one discovery step to find **and** (b) survives the
   next upstream merge. Anything task-specific, sprint-specific or personal goes to `ai-logs/`.
4. No TODOs, no open questions, no first person, no dates other than `verified-at`.

**Form**
5. `_TEMPLATE.md` headings only, in order.
6. Hard cap **120 lines**. Over cap means the scope is too big: split it, and add the `INDEX.md`
   row in the same commit.
7. Every claim names a repo path. No path → delete the claim.
8. Code fences ≤ 10 lines. Cite `file.go:42` instead of quoting.
9. Repo-relative paths only — an absolute `/home/...` path fails the check.
10. No trailing whitespace (matches `AGENTS.md`).

**Change control**
11. One universal set, on `main` only. Never keep a personal variant, never a per-student folder.
12. Changes land by PR titled `docs(context): <subject>` — Conventional Commits per `AGENTS.md`,
    with the `Assisted-by:` trailer and no `Co-Authored-By`/`Signed-off-by`.
13. **Fix-in-place:** if you find a doc wrong while doing a task, correct it in that same PR and
    bump `verified-at`. Leaving it stale is the failure mode this folder exists to prevent.
14. A **new** doc requires, in one commit: the file, its `INDEX.md` row, and a non-overlapping
    `scope:`. If the scope overlaps an existing doc, edit that doc instead.
15. `./.claude-students/check.sh` passes before you push.

---

## `check.sh`

POSIX shell, no new dependencies, sub-second. Fails with `file:line message`. Checks:

- frontmatter present with `scope:` and `verified-at:`
- H2 set matches `_TEMPLATE.md` exactly, in order
- ≤ 120 lines; no code fence > 10 lines
- every `scope:` path exists in the repo; no path claimed by two docs
- every `docs/*.md` has an `INDEX.md` row and vice versa
- no absolute paths, no trailing whitespace

---

## Doc set — ~30 docs, priority-ordered into phases

**One phase per turn**, so token spend stays bounded and you can stop after any phase with a
coherent set. Order follows what course tasks actually touch (`STUDENTS.md` §5: code review UI,
issues/Kanban, CI/Actions).

**Phase 1 — scaffolding + spine.** `README.md`, `INDEX.md`, `MAINTENANCE.md`, `_TEMPLATE.md`,
`check.sh`, the two pointer edits, and the two most-read docs written as the reference examples:
- `architecture.md` — the `cmd → routers → services → models → modules` rule from
  `docs/guidelines-backend.md`, plural/singular package naming, snake_case import aliases
  (`issues_model`, `user_service`), and one end-to-end request trace
- `testing.md` — the 5 tiers and their harnesses: `models/unittest` (`MainTest`,
  `PrepareTestDatabase`, `CheckConsistencyFor`), `services/contexttest`, `tests/test_utils.go`
  (`PrepareTestEnv`), Vitest, Playwright, `make test-migration`; which tier to pick

**Phase 2 — request lifecycle.** `routers-web.md` (the `registerWebRoutes` table in
`routers/web/web.go:329` → handler → `templates.TplName`), `routers-api-v1.md` (guards in
`routers/api/v1/api.go`: `reqToken`/`reqRepoWriter`/`tokenRequiresScopes`, swagger comment block,
`modules/structs` + `routers/api/v1/swagger/` registration, method→status rules),
`services-context.md` (`Context`/`APIContext`, `RepoAssignment`, permissions, pagination; note
there is no `modules/context` in this tree), `services-forms-and-convert.md`

**Phase 3 — persistence.** `models-db.md` (`GetEngine`, `WithTx`/`WithTx2`, `RegisterModel`, the
XORM gotchas), `models-migrations.md` (append to the slice in `models/migrations/migrations.go`,
`v1_27/` subpackage, `minDBVersion`), `models-issues.md`, `models-repo-and-git.md`

**Phase 4 — issues / PR / review.** `services-issue.md`, `services-pull-and-gitdiff.md`,
`services-repository.md`, `models-project.md` (Kanban)

**Phase 5 — frontend.** `frontend-js.md` (`web_src/js/index.ts` → `callInitFunctions`, the
`initFoo()` contract, `features/`, `modules/fetch.ts`, `utils/dom.ts` show/hide),
`frontend-vue-components.md`, `frontend-css.md` (`tw-` prefix, `flex-*` over per-child margins,
`gt-`/`g-` helpers), `templates.md`

**Phase 6 — Actions / git.** `models-actions.md`, `services-actions.md`,
`routers-api-actions.md`, `modules-git.md`

**Phase 7 — modules.** `modules-setting.md`, `modules-structs.md`,
`modules-templates-and-markup.md`, `modules-util-and-generics.md` (the `util.Err*` sentinels and
the `ErrXxxNotExist`/`IsErrXxxNotExist`/`Unwrap` triad), `modules-infra.md` (queue, cache, storage,
indexer, log, globallock, graceful, reqctx, `modules/web`)

**Phase 8 — long tail** (trim freely if tokens run short). `models-user-org-perm.md`,
`services-user-org-auth.md`, `services-notify-mailer-webhook.md`, `models-packages.md`,
`routers-private-install-cmd.md`, `i18n.md` (edit only
`options/locale/locale_en-US.json`; rest come from Crowdin), `build-and-tooling.md`

---

## Verification

Per phase:
1. `./.claude-students/check.sh` → exits 0.
2. `git check-ignore -v .claude-students/INDEX.md` → exit 1 (still tracked).
3. `git status --short` → only `.claude-students/**` plus `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`; no other tracked
   file moved or modified.
4. **Accuracy spot-check:** for each new doc, open two paths it cites and confirm the claim. A doc
   that cannot be spot-checked from its own citations violates rule 7.
5. **Token payoff check:** in a fresh session, ask a question the doc should answer (e.g. "where do
   I register a new API route and what must the swagger block contain?"). It should be answered
   from the index + one doc, with no `grep` across the tree.

After Phase 1 only:
6. `make fmt` and `make lint-go` still clean — confirms nothing outside the folder was disturbed.
7. Removal rehearsal: `git stash` the pointer lines and confirm the repo is byte-identical to
   upstream apart from the untracked folder.

## Out of scope

- No nested `CLAUDE.md` files in `models/`, `services/` etc. — auto-loading isn't worth scattering
  course-only files through upstream directories.
- No `Makefile` target or CI job for `check.sh` (both would add hunt-and-remove surface).
- No changes to `STUDENTS.md`, `docs/`, or `ai-logs/`.

XORM gotchas), `models-migrations.md` (append to the slice in `models/migrations/migrations.go`,
`v1_27/` subpackage, `minDBVersion`), `models-issues.md`, `models-repo-and-git.md`

**Phase 4 — issues / PR / review.** `services-issue.md`, `services-pull-and-gitdiff.md`,
`services-repository.md`, `models-project.md` (Kanban)

**Phase 5 — frontend.** `frontend-js.md` (`web_src/js/index.ts` → `callInitFunctions`, the
`initFoo()` contract, `features/`, `modules/fetch.ts`, `utils/dom.ts` show/hide),
`frontend-vue-components.md`, `frontend-css.md` (`tw-` prefix, `flex-*` over per-child margins,
`gt-`/`g-` helpers), `templates.md`

**Phase 6 — Actions / git.** `models-actions.md`, `services-actions.md`,
`routers-api-actions.md`, `modules-git.md`

**Phase 7 — modules.** `modules-setting.md`, `modules-structs.md`,
`modules-templates-and-markup.md`, `modules-util-and-generics.md` (the `util.Err*` sentinels and
the `ErrXxxNotExist`/`IsErrXxxNotExist`/`Unwrap` triad), `modules-infra.md` (queue, cache, storage,
indexer, log, globallock, graceful, reqctx, `modules/web`)

**Phase 8 — long tail** (trim freely if tokens run short). `models-user-org-perm.md`,
`services-user-org-auth.md`, `services-notify-mailer-webhook.md`, `models-packages.md`,
`routers-private-install-cmd.md`, `i18n.md` (edit only
`options/locale/locale_en-US.json`; rest come from Crowdin), `build-and-tooling.md`

---

## Verification

Per phase:
1. `./.claude-students/check.sh` → exits 0.
2. `git check-ignore -v .claude-students/INDEX.md` → exit 1 (still tracked).
3. `git status --short` → only `.claude-students/**` plus `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`; no other tracked
   file moved or modified.
4. **Accuracy spot-check:** for each new doc, open two paths it cites and confirm the claim. A doc
   that cannot be spot-checked from its own citations violates rule 7.
5. **Token payoff check:** in a fresh session, ask a question the doc should answer (e.g. "where do
   I register a new API route and what must the swagger block contain?"). It should be answered
   from the index + one doc, with no `grep` across the tree.

After Phase 1 only:
6. `make fmt` and `make lint-go` still clean — confirms nothing outside the folder was disturbed.
7. Removal rehearsal: `git stash` the pointer lines and confirm the repo is byte-identical to
   upstream apart from the untracked folder.

## Out of scope

- No nested `CLAUDE.md` files in `models/`, `services/` etc. — auto-loading isn't worth scattering
  course-only files through upstream directories.
- No `Makefile` target or CI job for `check.sh` (both would add hunt-and-remove surface).
- No changes to `STUDENTS.md`, `docs/`, or `ai-logs/`.

# Maintenance rules

Five people maintain one shared set of docs. These rules exist so the set stays *one* set. Read
them before editing anything in `.claude-students/`. Rules marked **[checked]** are enforced by
`./.claude-students/check.sh`.

## Scope discipline

1. **Upstream wins.** `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/guidelines-*.md` are authoritative.
   Docs here summarise them and link to them; they never restate a rule differently and never
   contradict one. A contradiction is a bug in this folder, not in the project.
2. **One fact, one home.** Every fact lives in exactly one doc — the one whose `scope:` owns that
   path. Everywhere else, link to it. Duplicated facts are how five maintainers end up with five
   different answers.
3. **Durability test.** Record a fact only if it (a) took more than one discovery step to find and
   (b) will still be true after the next upstream merge. A one-off workaround, a sprint detail or
   anything about your own task fails this test — that belongs in `ai-logs/`.
4. **No process notes.** No TODOs, no open questions, no first person, no student names, no dates
   other than `verified-at`. This is a map of the code, not a journal.

## Form

5. **Template only [checked].** Use the `## ` headings from `_TEMPLATE.md`, all of them, in that
   order, with nothing added. If a section has nothing to say, write one line saying so.
6. **120-line cap [checked].** Going over means the scope is too broad. Split the doc, and add the
   new `INDEX.md` row in the same commit. `INDEX.md` itself is capped at 60 lines.
7. **Cite or delete [checked, partially].** Every claim names a repo path. A claim with no path is
   unverifiable by the next reader — delete it.
8. **Symbols, not line numbers [checked].** Write `models/db/context.go` → `WithTx`, never
   `models/db/context.go:143`. Line numbers rot at the next upstream merge and a stale number is
   worse than no number. Code fences stay at 10 lines or fewer — point at the file instead of
   copying it.
9. **Repo-relative paths [checked].** `models/db/context.go`, never `/home/you/gitea/models/...`.
10. **Whitespace [checked].** No trailing whitespace, LF endings, final newline — same as the rest
    of the repo (`.editorconfig`).

## Change control

11. **One universal set.** These docs live on `main` and nowhere else. Never keep a personal copy,
    a per-student folder, or a long-lived branch of them.
12. **Changes land by PR**, titled `docs(context): <subject>` per `AGENTS.md` Conventional Commits,
    with an `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer and no `Co-Authored-By` or
    `Signed-off-by`.
13. **Fix in place.** If you discover while working that a doc is wrong or incomplete, correct it
    in the *same* PR as your code change and update `verified-at` to the commit you checked
    against. Leaving a doc stale for someone else to hit is the exact failure this folder exists to
    prevent. This rule applies to AI sessions too.
14. **New docs need three things in one commit [checked]:** the file, its `INDEX.md` row, and a
    `scope:` that does not overlap any existing doc's. If the scope overlaps, you wanted to edit
    that doc, not add one.
15. **`./.claude-students/check.sh` passes before you push [checked].** It is dependency-free and
    finishes in under a second.

## Updating `verified-at`

`verified-at` is the short SHA the doc was last checked against, from `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.
Bump it whenever you confirm or correct a doc. A doc whose `verified-at` is far behind `main` has
not been checked recently — treat its details as hints and confirm them in the code before relying
on them.

---

verified-at: c0092050a4
---

# architecture — layers, dependency direction, request lifecycle

**Read when:** you are unsure which layer a change belongs in, which package to import, or how a
request reaches your handler.
**Not here:** per-package detail -> the doc for that path in `INDEX.md`; test tiers -> `testing.md`.

## Responsibilities

| Layer | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `cmd/` | CLI subcommands (`web`, `serv`, `hook`, `doctor`, `admin *`) |
| `routers/` | HTTP handlers, split into `web`, `api`, `private`, `install`, plus shared `common` |
| `services/` | business logic tying routers to models; also the request context and form binding |
| `models/` | XORM beans and database queries; keeps external dependencies to a minimum |
| `modules/` | standalone leaf utilities with few dependencies |
| `templates/` | Go `html/template` sources for server-rendered pages and mail |
| `web_src/` | frontend sources (TypeScript, Vue, CSS), built by vite into `public/assets/` |
| `options/` | shipped data: locales, gitignores, licenses, labels, readmes |

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `main.go` | binary entry point; wires the `cmd` subcommands |
| `routers/init.go` | `NormalRoutes` — mounts `/`, `/api/v1`, `/api/internal`, `/api/packages`, `/api/actions` |
| `routers/web/web.go` | `Routes` (middleware chain) and `registerWebRoutes` (the whole web route table) |
| `routers/api/v1/api.go` | `Routes` plus every API guard middleware |
| `services/context/context.go` | `Context`, the value every web handler receives |
| `modules/reqctx/datastore.go` | request-scoped key/value store underneath the context |
| `docs/guidelines-backend.md` | authoritative backend rules; this doc only summarises them |
| `docs/guidelines-refactoring.md` | process rules for when a refactor needs its own PR |

## Conventions & invariants

Dependencies flow one way only (`docs/guidelines-backend.md`):

```text
cmd → routers → services → models → modules
```

A package on the left may import a package on its right, but never the reverse. A backwards import
is the most common structural review rejection — move the code rather than adding the import.

- Top-level packages are plural (`services`, `models`, `routers`); subpackages are singular
  (`services/user`, `models/repo`).
- Cross-layer name collisions take a snake_case import alias: `issues_model`, `user_service`,
  `access_model`, and `api "gitea.dev/modules/structs"`. Match the aliases already used in the file
  you are editing.
- The module path in this fork is `gitea.dev`, **not** `code.gitea.io/gitea`. Copy import paths
  from a neighbouring file, not from upstream docs or search results.
- There is no `modules/context` in this tree. The request context lives in `services/context`
  because it has to depend on models and services.
- A function that participates in a transaction takes `context.Context` as its first parameter, so
  the transaction propagates. Never pass a `*xorm.Session` as a parameter.

## Recipes

**Decide where new code goes.** Does it read or write the database? `models/`. Does it coordinate
several model calls, or fan out to mail / notifications / webhooks? `services/`. Does it read the
request or write the response? `routers/`. Is it a pure helper with no Gitea dependencies?
`modules/`.

**Trace a web request.** `routers/init.go` (`NormalRoutes`) → `routers/web/web.go` (`Routes` builds
the middleware chain; `registerWebRoutes` matches the path) → a handler in
`routers/web/{repo,user,org,admin,auth,explore}/` with signature `func(ctx *context.Context)` →
services → models → the handler fills `ctx.Data[...]` and calls `ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplFoo)`,
where `tplFoo` is a package-level `templates.TplName` naming a file under `templates/`.

**Trace an API request.** The same until `routers/api/v1/api.go`, then a handler
`func(ctx *context.APIContext)` that converts models to a `modules/structs` type and returns it
with `ctx.JSON`.

## Gotchas

- Run `make fmt` before committing, `make lint-go` / `make lint-js` before pushing, and `make tidy`
  after any `go.mod` change (`AGENTS.md`). `make help` lists every target.
- Changing a struct under `models/` that is persisted to the database almost always requires a new
  migration in `models/migrations/`.
- `templates/` and `web_src/` sit outside the dependency rule, but a template may only use data the
  handler actually put in `ctx.Data`.
- `docs/guidelines-refactoring.md` limits refactor scope: fix the root cause, keep the PR tight,
  and split large refactors across PRs.

## Related

- `testing.md` — which test tier to write and how to set it up
- `docs/guidelines-backend.md`, `docs/guidelines-frontend.md` — the authoritative rules
EOF

---
scope: docs/testing.md, models/unittest, models/fixtures, services/contexttest, tests
verified-at: c0092050a4
---

# testing — the five tiers and their harnesses

**Read when:** choosing what kind of test to write, or a test needs a database, a request context,
a git repo or a fixture.
**Not here:** lint and build targets -> `architecture.md` Gotchas.

## Responsibilities

| Tier | Lives in | Runner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Go unit | `*_test.go` beside the code | `make test-backend` |
| Frontend unit | `*.test.ts` beside the source | `make test-frontend` |
| Integration | `tests/integration/` | `make test-integration` |
| E2E (browser) | `tests/e2e/*.test.ts` | `make test-e2e` |
| Migration | `models/migrations/` | `make test-migration` |

Prefer a unit test whenever the logic is testable in isolation (`AGENTS.md`). Integration and e2e
tests should stay under roughly 2s locally, so push setup-heavy cases down a tier where you can.
Fuzz targets live in `tests/fuzz/`.

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `models/unittest/testdb.go` | `MainTest`, `TestOptions`, `PrepareTestDatabase` — the unit-test DB harness |
| `models/unittest/unit_tests.go` | `AssertExistsAndLoadBean`, and the other assertion helpers |
| `models/unittest/consistency.go` | `CheckConsistencyFor` — verifies counter columns match rows |
| `models/fixtures/*.yml` | 78 seed files, one per table (`issue.yml`, `repository.yml`, `user.yml`) |
| `services/contexttest/context_tests.go` | `MockContext`, `MockAPIContext`, `MockPrivateContext` for handler-level tests |
| `tests/test_utils.go` | `InitIntegrationTest`, `PrepareTestEnv`, `PrintCurrentTest`, the storage `Prepare*` helpers |
| `tests/integration/integration_test.go` | `TestMain` for the whole integration suite |
| `tests/gitea-repositories-meta/`, `tests/gitea-lfs-meta/`, `tests/testdata/` | pre-built git repos and LFS data |
| `tests/e2e/utils.ts` | shared Playwright helpers; config in `playwright.config.ts` |
| `web_src/js/vitest.setup.ts`, `web_src/js/utils/testhelper.ts` | Vitest setup and helpers; config in `vitest.config.ts` |
| `docs/testing.md` | authoritative test documentation; this doc summarises it |

## Conventions & invariants

- A Go package whose tests touch the database needs a `main_test.go` containing
  `func TestMain(m *testing.M) { unittest.MainTest(m) }`. Without it the test DB is never
  initialised.
- Every DB-backed test calls `unittest.PrepareTestDatabase()` first, which reloads the fixtures, so
  tests do not depend on each other's writes.
- Adding a row to `models/fixtures/*.yml` means keeping denormalised counter columns
  (`num_issues`, `num_closed_issues`, ...) consistent, or `CheckConsistencyFor` fails.
- Handler tests use `contexttest.MockContext` rather than constructing a `context.Context`
  by hand — see `services/context` for what the real one carries.
- Integration tests need Git LFS installed. The database comes from `GITEA_TEST_DATABASE`; empty
  defaults to SQLite, which is what you want locally.
- Frontend tests are Vitest, not Jest. Playwright is only for the e2e tier.

## Recipes

**Run one test.**

```sh
go test -run '^TestName$' ./modulepath/   # or: make test-backend#TestName
pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>
GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='<filepath>' make test-e2e
```

**Add a DB-backed unit test.** Put `*_test.go` beside the code; add `main_test.go` with
`unittest.MainTest(m)` if the package has none; call `unittest.PrepareTestDatabase()`; load rows
with `unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean`; add fixture rows only if no existing row fits.

**Add an integration test.** New `tests/integration/xxx_test.go`; `defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()`
at the top of the test; drive it through HTTP the way the neighbouring tests do. Do not add a
`TestMain` — `integration_test.go` already owns it.

**Add a migration test.** Alongside the migration in `models/migrations/`, with its own fixtures
under `models/migrations/fixtures/`; helpers in `models/migrations/migrationtest/`.

## Gotchas

- `GITEA_TEST_LOG_SQL=1` logs every SQL statement — the fastest way to see what a failing DB test
  actually queried.
- `GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR` multiplies e2e timeouts (default 4 on CI, 1 locally); a test that
  only passes with a raised factor is a flaky test, not a slow machine.
- A handful of Go unit tests fail on native Windows for platform reasons (symlinks, temp-file
  cleanup). Run the suite on Linux, macOS, WSL2 or the `.devcontainer` (`STUDENTS.md` §6).
- `tests/integration` and `tests/e2e` share one Gitea instance per run, so a test that leaves state
  behind breaks later tests rather than itself.

## Related

- `architecture.md` — which layer the code under test belongs to
- `docs/testing.md` — full documentation, including non-SQLite database setup

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Validates .claude-students against the mechanical rules in MAINTENANCE.md.
# Dependency-free. Run from anywhere: ./.claude-students/check.sh
set -uo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1

DIR=".claude-students"
TEMPLATE="$DIR/_TEMPLATE.md"
INDEX="$DIR/INDEX.md"
MAX_LINES=120
MAX_INDEX_LINES=60
MAX_FENCE=10

fail=0
err() {
  printf '%s: %s\n' "$1" "$2" >&2
  fail=1
}

for required in "$TEMPLATE" "$INDEX" "$DIR/MAINTENANCE.md" "$DIR/README.md"; do
  [ -f "$required" ] || err "$required" "missing"
done
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1

check_whitespace() {
  local file="$1" line
  line=$(grep -n '[[:space:]]$' "$file" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  [ -z "$line" ] || err "$file:$line" "trailing whitespace (rule 10)"
  [ -z "$(tail -c 1 "$file")" ] || err "$file" "no final newline (rule 10)"
}

for meta in "$TEMPLATE" "$INDEX" "$DIR/MAINTENANCE.md" "$DIR/README.md"; do
  check_whitespace "$meta"
done

want_h2=$(grep '^## ' "$TEMPLATE")

index_lines=$(wc -l < "$INDEX")
if [ "$index_lines" -gt "$MAX_INDEX_LINES" ]; then
  err "$INDEX" "$index_lines lines, cap is $MAX_INDEX_LINES (rule 6)"
fi

claimed=""
found_doc=0

for doc in "$DIR"/docs/*.md; do
  [ -e "$doc" ] || break
  found_doc=1
  name="${doc##*/}"

  lines=$(wc -l < "$doc")
  if [ "$lines" -gt "$MAX_LINES" ]; then
    err "$doc" "$lines lines, cap is $MAX_LINES - split it (rule 6)"
  fi

  check_whitespace "$doc"

  if [ "$(head -1 "$doc")" != "---" ]; then
    err "$doc:1" "must open with a --- frontmatter block (rule 5)"
  fi

  scope_line=$(sed -n '2,10{/^scope:/p;}' "$doc")
  [ -n "$scope_line" ] || err "$doc" "frontmatter has no scope: (rule 14)"
  [ -n "$(sed -n '2,10{/^verified-at:/p;}' "$doc")" ] ||
    err "$doc" "frontmatter has no verified-at: (rule 13)"

  got_h2=$(grep '^## ' "$doc")
  if [ "$got_h2" != "$want_h2" ]; then
    err "$doc" "## headings must match _TEMPLATE.md exactly and in order (rule 5)"
  fi

  long_fence=$(awk -v max="$MAX_FENCE" '
    /^```/ {
      if (open) { if (NR - start - 1 > max) print start; open = 0 }
      else { open = 1; start = NR }
    }
  ' "$doc" | head -1)
  [ -z "$long_fence" ] ||
    err "$doc:$long_fence" "code fence over $MAX_FENCE lines - cite the file instead (rule 8)"

  lineref=$(grep -nE '\.(go|ts|vue|tmpl|css|md|yml|json):[0-9]+' "$doc" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  [ -z "$lineref" ] ||
    err "$doc:$lineref" "cites a line number - use the symbol name instead (rule 8)"

  abspath=$(grep -nE '(^|[[:space:]`(])(/home/|/Users/|/root/|[A-Za-z]:\\)' "$doc" |
    head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  [ -z "$abspath" ] || err "$doc:$abspath" "absolute path - use a repo-relative one (rule 9)"

  grep -q "docs/$name" "$INDEX" || err "$INDEX" "no row pointing at docs/$name (rule 14)"

  while read -r path; do
    [ -n "$path" ] || continue
    [ -e "$path" ] || err "$doc" "scope path does not exist: $path (rule 7)"
    owner=$(printf '%s' "$claimed" | awk -F'|' -v p="$path" '$1 == p { print $2; exit }')
    if [ -n "$owner" ]; then
      err "$doc" "scope path $path is already owned by docs/$owner (rule 2)"
    else
      claimed="${claimed}${path}|${name}
"
    fi
  done < <(printf '%s' "${scope_line#scope:}" | tr ',' '\n' |
    sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//')
done

[ "$found_doc" -eq 1 ] || err "$DIR/docs" "contains no docs"

while read -r ref; do
  [ -f "$DIR/$ref" ] || err "$INDEX" "points at $ref, which does not exist (rule 14)"
done < <(grep -oE 'docs/[a-z0-9.-]+\.md' "$INDEX" | sort -u)

if [ "$fail" -eq 0 ]; then
  printf 'check.sh: ok (%s docs)\n' "$(find "$DIR/docs" -name '*.md' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
fi
exit "$fail"
SCRIPT
chmod +x .claude-students/check.sh
./.claude-students/check.sh; echo "exit=$?"
````

Those rot at the next upstream merge, and a stale line number is worse than none — so docs cite `models/db/context.go` → `WithTx` instead, and `check.sh` rejects any `.go:123`-style reference. This survives your semester of upstream merges; line numbers wouldn't.

**`check.sh` had a real bug, caught by negative-testing it.** `printf '%s'` emits no trailing newline, so `while read` silently dropped the **last** scope path of every doc — rule 2 (one fact, one home) and rule 7 were skipping it, and a single-path doc was skipped entirely. func Routes() *web.Router {
	routes := web.NewRouter()

	// GetHead allows a HEAD request redirect to GET if HEAD method is not defined for that route
	routes.BeforeRouting(chi_middleware.GetHead)

	routes.Head("/", misc.DummyOK) // for health check - doesn't need to be passed through gzip handler
	routes.Methods("GET, HEAD", "/assets/site-manifest.json", misc.SiteManifest)
	routes.Methods("GET, HEAD, OPTIONS", "/assets/*", routing.MarkLogLevelTrace, public.AssetsCors(), public.FileHandlerFunc())
	routes.Methods("GET, HEAD", "/avatars/*", avatarStorageHandler(setting.Avatar.Storage, "avatars", storage.Avatars))
	routes.Methods("GET, HEAD", "/repo-avatars/*", avatarStorageHandler(setting.RepoAvatar.Storage, "repo-avatars", storage.RepoAvatars))
	routes.Methods("GET, HEAD", "/apple-touch-icon.png", misc.StaticRedirect("/assets/img/apple-touch-icon.png"))
	routes.Methods("GET, HEAD", "/apple-touch-icon-precomposed.png", misc.StaticRedirect("/assets/img/apple-touch-icon.png"))
	routes.Methods("GET, HEAD", "/favicon.ico", misc.StaticRedirect("/assets/img/favicon.png"))

	var mid []any

	if setting.EnableGzip {
		// random jitter is recommended by: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/klauspost/compress/gzhttp#readme-breach-mitigation
		// compression level 6 is the gzip default and a good general tradeoff between speed, CPU usage, and compression
		wrapper, err := gzhttp.NewWrapper(gzhttp.RandomJitter(32, 0, false), gzhttp.MinSize(GzipMinSize), gzhttp.CompressionLevel(6))
		if err != nil {
			log.Fatal("gzhttp.NewWrapper failed: %v", err)
		}
		mid = append(mid, wrapper)
	}

	if setting.Service.EnableCaptcha {
		// The captcha http.Handler should only fire on /captcha/* so we can just mount this on that url
		routes.Methods("GET,HEAD", "/captcha/*", append(mid, captcha.Captchaer(context.GetImageCaptcha()))...)
	}

	if setting.Metrics.Enabled {
		prometheus.MustRegister(metrics.NewCollector())
		routes.Get("/metrics", append(mid, Metrics)...)
	}

	routes.Methods("GET,HEAD", "/robots.txt", append(mid, misc.RobotsTxt)...)
	routes.Get("/ssh_info", misc.SSHInfo)
	routes.Get("/api/healthz", healthcheck.Check)

	mid = append(mid, common.MustInitSessioner(), context.Contexter())

	// Get user from session if logged in.
	webAuth := newWebAuthMiddleware()
	mid = append(mid, webAuth.MiddlewareHandler)

	if setting.API.EnableSwagger {
		// Note: The route is here but no in API routes because it renders a web page
		routes.Get("/api/swagger", append(mid, misc.Swagger)...) // Render V1 by default
	}

	mid = append(mid, goGet)
	mid = append(mid, common.PageGlobalData)
	mid = append(mid, common.BlockExpensive(), common.QoS(), web.RouterMockPoint(RouterMockPointBeforeWebRoutes))

	webRoutes := web.NewRouter()
	webRoutes.AfterRouting(mid...)
	registerWebRoutes(webRoutes, webAuth)

	routes.Mount("", webRoutes)
	return routes
}

// optSignInFromAnyOrigin means that the user can (optionally) be signed in from any origin (no cross-origin protection)
//   - With CORS middleware: CORS middleware does the preflight request handling, the requests has Sec-Fetch-Site header.
//     The CORS mechanism already protects cross-origin requests, and the CrossOriginProtection has no "allowed origin" list, so disable CrossOriginProtection.
//   - For non-browser client requests: git clone via http, no Sec-Fetch-Site header.
//     Such requests are not cross-origin requests, so disable CrossOriginProtection.
var optSignInFromAnyOrigin = verifyAuthWithOptions(&common.VerifyOptions{DisableCrossOriginProtection: true})

=== guidelines-backend API section ===
## API v1

The API is documented with [Swagger](https://gitea.com/api/swagger) and is modelled
on [the GitHub API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest).

### GitHub API compatibility

Gitea's API should use the same endpoints and fields as the GitHub API where
possible, unless there is a good reason to deviate.

- If Gitea offers functionality GitHub does not, a new endpoint may be added.
- If Gitea exposes information the GitHub API does not, a new field may be added as
  long as it does not collide with a GitHub field.
- Existing fields should not be removed unless there is a strong reason; the same
  applies to status responses.

If you notice a problem that would require a breaking change, leave a comment in the
code for a future refactor to API v2 (which is currently not planned) rather than
breaking v1.

### Adding and maintaining API routes

- All possible results (errors, success, and failure messages) must be documented in
  the swagger comments on the route.
- Every JSON request body must be defined as a struct in `modules/structs/` and
  registered in [`routers/api/v1/swagger/options.go`](../routers/api/v1/swagger/options.go).
- Every JSON response must be defined as a struct in `modules/structs/` and
  registered with its category under [`routers/api/v1/swagger/`](../routers/api/v1/swagger).

### HTTP methods and status codes

In general, choose HTTP methods as follows:

- **GET** returns the requested object(s) with status **200 OK**.
- **POST** creates a new object (e.g. a user) and returns **201 Created** with the
  created object.
- **PUT** adds or assigns an existing object (e.g. a user to a team) and returns
  **204 No Content** with no body.
- **PATCH** edits an existing object and returns the changed object with **200 OK**.
- **DELETE** removes an object and returns **204 No Content** with no body.

### Requirements for API routes

- All parameters of endpoints that edit an object must be optional, except those
  needed to identify the object, which are required.

---
scope: routers/web, routers/common, modules/web
verified-at: c0092050a4
---

# routers/web — the HTML route table and page handlers

**Read when:** adding or changing a page, a form POST, or a guard on a web route.
**Not here:** the `ctx` value itself -> `services-context.md`; form structs -> `services-forms-and-convert.md`; JSON endpoints -> `routers-api-v1.md`.

## Responsibilities

- `routers/web/web.go` — `Routes` assembles the middleware chain; `registerWebRoutes` declares
  every HTML route in nested `m.Group` blocks.
- `routers/web/{repo,user,org,admin,auth,explore,feed,events,misc,healthcheck,devtest,shared}/` —
  the handlers themselves. `events` is the server-sent-events endpoint; `devtest` is the
  `/devtest` component gallery.
- `routers/common/` — middleware and helpers shared with the API layer.
- `modules/web/` — a thin chi wrapper: `NewRouter`, `BeforeRouting`, `AfterRouting`, `Mount`,
  `Bind`, `GetForm`.

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `routers/web/web.go` | `Routes`, `registerWebRoutes`, `verifyAuthWithOptions` |
| `routers/web/repo/issue.go` | a representative handler set, and the `templates.TplName` constants |
| `routers/common/pagetmpl.go` | `PageGlobalData` — data every template can rely on |
| `routers/common/middleware.go` | `MustInitSessioner` |
| `routers/common/blockexpensive.go`, `qos.go` | `BlockExpensive`, `QoS` load shedding |
| `routers/common/errpage.go` | the panic/error page renderer |
| `modules/web/router.go` | `Bind`, `GetForm` |

## Conventions & invariants

- A handler is `func Foo(ctx *context.Context)` from `gitea.dev/services/context`. It puts data in
  `ctx.Data`, then calls `ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplFoo)`.
- `tplFoo` is a package-level `templates.TplName` constant whose value is a path under `templates/`
  without the extension — `tplIssues templates.TplName = "repo/issue/list"`.
- `ctx.Data` is the only channel from handler to template. A template cannot reach anything the
  handler did not put there.
- Sign-in guards are local variables built at the top of `registerWebRoutes` from
  `verifyAuthWithOptions`: `reqSignIn`, `reqSignOut`, `optSignIn`, `optExploreSignIn`. A new guard
  is declared there too, not in a subpackage.
- Repo pages get `context.RepoAssignment` (see `services-context.md`), which fills `ctx.Repo`;
  ref-scoped pages add `context.RepoRefByType`.
- A POST that takes a form is registered as
  `m.Post("/path", web.Bind(forms.XxxForm{}), handler)`; the handler reads it back with
  `web.GetForm(ctx)`.
- The middleware chain in `Routes` is, in order: `chi_middleware.GetHead`, optional gzip,
  `common.MustInitSessioner`, `context.Contexter`, the web auth middleware, `goGet`,
  `common.PageGlobalData`, then `common.BlockExpensive` and `common.QoS`.

## Recipes

**Add a page.**

1. Handler in the matching `routers/web/<area>/` file, signature `func(ctx *context.Context)`.
2. A `templates.TplName` constant beside the other constants in that file.
3. The template file at the matching path under `templates/`.
4. The route inside the right `m.Group` in `registerWebRoutes`, with the guards that group needs.
5. Any user-visible string as a key in `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` — never a literal.

**Add a form POST.** Do the above, plus a form struct in `services/forms/` and `web.Bind` on the
route. See `services-forms-and-convert.md`.

## Gotchas

- The static routes registered on `routes` *before* the `mid` slice is assembled (`/assets/*`,
  `/avatars/*`, `/favicon.ico`, `/api/healthz`) deliberately bypass session and auth middleware.
  Do not add an authenticated route there.
- `registerWebRoutes` is long. Find your group by URL prefix rather than reading top to bottom, and
  add the route to the group that already carries the guards you need instead of re-listing them.
- `ctx.HTML` after something has already written the response is a bug; `ctx.Written()` reports
  whether that happened.

## Related

- `services-context.md` — what `ctx` carries and the response helpers
- `routers-api-v1.md` — the JSON side of the same handlers
- `architecture.md` — where routing sits in the dependency direction

---

# routers/api/v1 — the REST API, its guards and its swagger spec

**Read when:** adding or changing a `/api/v1` endpoint, or a swagger check fails.
**Not here:** HTML routes -> `routers-web.md`; `ctx` itself -> `services-context.md`; DTO conversion -> `services-forms-and-convert.md`.

## Responsibilities

- `routers/api/v1/api.go` — `Routes` declares every v1 endpoint and defines every guard middleware.
- `routers/api/v1/{repo,org,user,admin,notify,packages,settings,misc,activitypub,token}/` — the
  handlers.
- `routers/api/v1/swagger/` — registers request and response structs so go-swagger emits their
  definitions.
- `routers/api/v1/utils/` — shared helpers, including pagination.

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `routers/api/v1/api.go` | `Routes`, and all the `req*` / `must*` / `bind` middleware |
| `routers/api/v1/repo/issue.go` | representative handlers with full swagger comment blocks |
| `routers/api/v1/swagger/options.go` | `swaggerParameterBodies` — every request body must be listed here |
| `routers/api/v1/swagger/issue.go` | response registration, one file per category |
| `routers/api/v1/utils/hook.go` | example of `ctx.SetTotalCountHeader` on a list endpoint |

## Conventions & invariants

From `docs/guidelines-backend.md` (authoritative — read it before designing an endpoint):

- Mirror the GitHub API's endpoints and field names where possible. Extra endpoints and fields are
  fine when Gitea offers something GitHub does not; removing or renaming an existing field is not.
- **Never break v1.** If a fix would be breaking, leave a code comment for a hypothetical v2
  instead.
- **Every** result — success, failure and each error — must appear in the swagger comment block.
- Every JSON request body is a struct in `modules/structs/` **and** listed in
  `routers/api/v1/swagger/options.go`. Every JSON response is a struct in `modules/structs/` **and**
  registered by category under `routers/api/v1/swagger/`. Miss either and the spec is incomplete.
- Method to status: GET → 200 with the object; POST → 201 with the created object; PUT → 204 with
  no body; PATCH → 200 with the changed object; DELETE → 204 with no body.
- On an edit endpoint every parameter is optional except the ones identifying the object.
- List endpoints accept `page` and `limit` and call `ctx.SetTotalCountHeader` so `X-Total-Count`
  is set.

Handler shape: `func Foo(ctx *context.APIContext)`, converting models with `services/convert`
before `ctx.JSON`. The swagger block sits immediately above the handler body and opens with
`// swagger:operation <METHOD> <path> <tag> <operationId>` followed by `// ---`.

## Recipes

**Add an endpoint.**

1. If it takes a body: an option struct in `modules/structs/`, then add it to
   `swaggerParameterBodies` in `routers/api/v1/swagger/options.go`.
2. If it returns something new: a struct in `modules/structs/`, registered in the matching
   `routers/api/v1/swagger/<category>.go`.
3. The handler in the right subpackage, with the complete swagger comment block.
4. The route in `api.go`, inside the group whose guards you need, adding `reqToken()`,
   `tokenRequiresScopes(...)` and `bind(api.XxxOption{})` as appropriate.
5. `make generate-swagger`, and commit the regenerated `templates/swagger/v1_json.tmpl`.

**Pick guards.** Authentication: `reqToken`, `reqBasicOrRevProxyAuth`, `tokenRequiresScopes`.
Repo access: `repoAssignment()`, `reqRepoReader(unit)`, `reqRepoWriter(units...)`,
`reqAnyRepoReader`. Org access: `orgAssignment()`, `reqOrgMembership`, `reqOrgOwnership`,
`reqTeamMembership`. Admin: `reqSiteAdmin`, `reqOwner`, `reqAdmin`, `reqSelfOrAdmin`. Feature
gates: `mustEnableIssues`, `mustAllowPulls`, `mustEnableWiki`, `mustNotBeArchived`,
`mustEnableEditor`, `mustEnableAttachments`.

## Gotchas

- `make swagger-check` fails CI when the committed spec does not match the comments, so a swagger
  block edit always means regenerating and committing `templates/swagger/v1_json.tmpl`.
- The `swagger:parameters parameterBodies` annotation in `options.go` matches no real route on
  purpose — it exists only to force go-swagger to emit the definitions. Add to the struct; do not
  "fix" the annotation.
- `bind` here is the API-local helper in `api.go` over `modules/structs` types. The web layer's
  `web.Bind` over `services/forms` types is a different mechanism.
- A guard added to a group applies to every route in it — check the group before adding a
  per-route guard that is already there.

## Related

- `routers-web.md` — the HTML side and the shared middleware in `routers/common`
- `services-forms-and-convert.md` — `services/convert` turns models into these DTOs

# services/context — the request context every handler receives

**Read when:** you need something off `ctx`, need to fail a request correctly, or a handler needs
repo/org/user assignment.
**Not here:** route registration -> `routers-web.md` and `routers-api-v1.md`; mocking it in tests -> `testing.md`.

## Responsibilities

Three context types, all built on the shared `Base`:

| Type | File | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Context` | `services/context/context.go` | web/HTML handlers |
| `APIContext` | `services/context/api.go` | `/api/v1` handlers |
| `PrivateContext` | `services/context/private.go` | the internal API `routers/private` |

It also owns the assignment middleware that resolves the URL into loaded models
(`ctx.Repo`, `ctx.Org`, `ctx.Package`, `ctx.ContextUser`) and the permission checks over them.

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `services/context/context.go` | `Context`, `Contexter` (the middleware that creates it), `JSONError` |
| `services/context/base.go` | `Base` — `JSON`, `HTTPError`, `PlainText`, `Redirect`, `SetTotalCountHeader`, `Tr`, `TrN`, `Written` |
| `services/context/context_response.go` | `HTML`, `NotFound`, `ServerError`, `NotFoundOrServerError`, `RedirectToCurrentSite` |
| `services/context/repo.go` | `Repository` struct, `RepoAssignment`, `RepoRefByType`, `RepoRefByDefaultBranch` |
| `services/context/permission.go` | the unit/access-mode guards over `ctx.Repo.Permission` |
| `services/context/pagination.go` | `NewPagination` |
| `services/context/org.go`, `user.go`, `package.go` | the other assignment middlewares |
| `services/context/upload/` | multipart upload handling |
| `modules/reqctx/datastore.go` | the request-scoped key/value store `ctx.Data` is built on |

## Conventions & invariants

- There is **no `modules/context`** in this tree. The context lives in `services/` because it
  depends on models and services. Import paths copied from upstream Gitea docs will be wrong.
- `ctx.Data` (type `reqctx.ContextData`) carries values to templates. `ctx.PageData` is separate:
  it becomes `window.config.pageData` for frontend modules.
- `ctx.Doer` is the signed-in user; `ctx.ContextUser` is the user being *viewed*. They differ on
  most profile and org pages — conflating them is a recurring permission bug.
- `ctx.Repo` is a `context.Repository`, not a `repo_model.Repository`. The model is
  `ctx.Repo.Repository`; permissions are `ctx.Repo.Permission`; the opened git repo is
  `ctx.Repo.GitRepo`. `RefFullName`, `BranchName`, `TreePath`, `Commit` and `CommitID` are only
  populated when a `RepoRef*` middleware ran.
- Fail a request through the helpers, never by writing the response yourself: `ctx.NotFound`,
  `ctx.ServerError`, `ctx.NotFoundOrServerError` (which picks between them from an error check),
  `ctx.HTTPError` for a bare status. They log and render consistently.
- Anything a handler puts on `ctx` lives for one request only.

## Recipes

**Get the current user and repo.** `ctx.Doer` and `ctx.Repo.Repository`, but only after the route
carries the matching guard — `optSignIn`/`reqSignIn` for the doer (`routers-web.md`),
`context.RepoAssignment` for the repo.

**Return an error correctly.** A missing row is `ctx.NotFound(err)`. An unexpected failure is
`ctx.ServerError("what failed", err)`. When the same error could be either, pass the model's
`IsErrXxxNotExist` to `ctx.NotFoundOrServerError`.

**Paginate a list page.** Build a `context.NewPagination(total, pageSize, page, numPages)`, put it
in `ctx.Data["Page"]`, and render `templates/base/paginate.tmpl`.

## Gotchas

- Adding a field to `Context` costs memory on every request and is almost never right — put it in
  `ctx.Data` instead.
- `ctx.Tr` returns `template.HTML`, so it is already escaped. Do not escape it again.
- After any helper that writes the response, return immediately. `ctx.Written()` exists for the
  cases where you cannot tell.

## Related

- `routers-web.md`, `routers-api-v1.md` — where the assignment middleware is attached
- `testing.md` — `contexttest.MockContext` for handler-level tests

# services/forms and services/convert — request in, DTO out

**Read when:** adding a form POST to a web page, or returning a model through the API.
**Not here:** route registration -> `routers-web.md` / `routers-api-v1.md`; the DTO structs themselves live in `modules/structs`.

## Responsibilities

- `services/forms/` — one struct per HTML form, with binding and validation rules. Used only by
  the web layer.
- `services/convert/` — turns model structs into the `modules/structs` API types. Used by the API
  layer, and anywhere else an API-shaped payload is needed (webhooks, notifications).

The API layer does **not** use `services/forms`: it binds `modules/structs` option types directly.

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `services/forms/repo_form.go` | the repo/issue/PR forms, e.g. `CreateIssueForm` |
| `services/forms/user_form.go`, `auth_form.go`, `org.go`, `admin.go` | forms for the other areas |
| `services/convert/convert.go` | the general converters (`ToEmail`, `ToBranch`, `ToTag`, ...) |
| `services/convert/issue.go` | `ToAPIIssue`, `ToAPIIssueList`, `ToLabel`, `ToTrackedTime` |
| `services/convert/pull.go`, `pull_review.go`, `repository.go`, `user.go` | one file per domain |
| `modules/web/middleware/binding.go` | `Validate`, which every form's `Validate` delegates to |
| `modules/validation/binding.go` | `AddBindingRules` — registers the custom binding rules |

## Conventions & invariants

**Forms**

- A form is a plain struct with `binding:"..."` tags: `binding:"Required;MaxSize(255)"`. Field
  names map from the request automatically; add `form:"assignee_ids"` only when the request field
  name differs from the Go field name.
- A form that needs the standard error handling implements
  `Validate(req *http.Request, errs binding.Errors) binding.Errors` and returns
  `middleware.Validate(errs, ctx.Data, f, ctx.Locale)` — copy the body from a neighbouring form
  verbatim; it is boilerplate, not a decision.
- Validation messages are locale keys, resolved through `ctx.Locale` by `middleware.Validate`.
  `validation.AddBindingRules` is called once from `registerWebRoutes` and registers the custom
  rules; a new rule goes there, not into the form.
- The route wires the form with `web.Bind(forms.XxxForm{})` and the handler reads it back with
  `web.GetForm(ctx)`, type-asserted to the form type.

**Converters**

- Naming is `To<Thing>` for the plain conversion and `To<Thing>List` for a slice. Where both an
  internal and an API-facing variant exist, the API one is `ToAPI<Thing>`.
- Signature convention is `ToXxx(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, model *T) *api.T` —
  `doer` is present because the output is permission-dependent, so pass the real doer, never `nil`,
  unless the neighbouring call sites do.
- Converters return `modules/structs` types. They must not query for anything a caller could have
  loaded; a converter that fans out queries per item turns a list endpoint into an N+1.

## Recipes

**Add a field to a form.** Add the struct field with its `binding` tag, add the locale key for any
new validation message to `options/locale/locale_en-US.json`, then read it in the handler from
`web.GetForm(ctx)`. Existing forms have tests in `services/forms/repo_form_test.go` — extend them
rather than adding an integration test.

**Expose a new model field over the API.** Add the field to the `modules/structs` type, set it in
the matching `services/convert` function, and check whether the swagger response registration in
`routers/api/v1/swagger/` already covers the struct (it usually does). Then
`make generate-swagger`.

## Gotchas

- Two binding mechanisms with similar names: `web.Bind` (web, `services/forms` types) and the
  local `bind` helper in `routers/api/v1/api.go` (API, `modules/structs` types). Using the web one
  on an API route silently binds nothing useful.
- `web.GetForm` returns `any`. A wrong type assertion panics at request time, not compile time —
  match the type in `web.Bind` exactly.
- Adding a field to a `modules/structs` type without setting it in the converter ships a field
  that is always the zero value, and swagger will still document it as present.

## Related

- `routers-web.md` — where `web.Bind` is attached
- `routers-api-v1.md` — the swagger registration these DTOs need

`INDEX.md` is now 17 lines (cap 60). Footprint outside the folder is still exactly 2 lines.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `check.sh` | ok (6 docs) — no scope overlaps across all 6 |
| 46 cited paths | all exist |
| Symbols (`PrivateContext`, `APIContext`, `reqctx.ContextData`, `PageData`) | confirmed in source |
| tabs / CRLF / trailing whitespace | clean |
| `git diff --stat` | still 2 insertions |

## Three claims I had to correct during the spot-check

Worth flagging because they're the kind of thing that would have misled someone later:

1. **`ToXxx` signatures aren't uniform.** I'd written the `(ctx, doer, model)` shape as *the* convention. `convert.go`'s `ToEmail` and `ToTag` take neither. Now split: permission-dependent converters take `ctx`/`doer`, pure value conversions take just the model.
2. **`permission.go` contents.** I'd described it vaguely as "unit/access-mode guards"; it actually exports `RequireRepoAdmin`, `RequireUnitWriter`, `RequireUnitReader`, `CanWriteToBranch` plus token-scope checks. Named them.
3. **`templates/base/paginate.tmpl`** is not used by `repo/issue/list.tmpl` as I'd implied — its consumers are the `templates/admin/*` lists. The pagination recipe now cites `routers/web/explore/repo.go` for the `ctx.Data["Page"]` half, which I did verify.

## Two things these docs capture that cost real discovery time

- **There is no `modules/context`** in this tree — it's `services/context`. Any import path copied from upstream Gitea docs or a search result will be wrong.
- **Two similarly-named binding mechanisms**: `web.Bind` (web layer, `services/forms` types) vs. the local `bind` helper in `api.go` (API layer, `modules/structs` types). Using the wrong one binds nothing useful and fails at request time, not compile time.

Say the word for Phase 3 (`models-db.md`, `models-migrations.md`, `models-issues.md`, `models-repo-and-git.md`).
